def flows(self, view: str = "realized") -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return one row per goods/process edge in one graph view."""
    narrowed = validate_view(view)
    graph = self._source_graph(narrowed)
    in_cycle = cyclic_nodes(graph)
    rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    for source, target, data in sorted(graph.edges(data=True)):
        rows.append(
            {

def constraints(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return named LP constraint values, slacks, and solver marginals."""
    levels = self.state.building_levels
    rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []

    def append_blocks(
        kind: Literal["inequality", "equality"],
        matrix: np.ndarray | None,
        bounds: np.ndarray | None,
        slices: ConstraintSlices,
        marginals: np.ndarray | None,
    ) -> None:
        if matrix is None or bounds is None:
            return
        values = matrix @ levels
        for family, row_slice in slices.items():
            start = 0 if row_slice.start is None else row_slice.start
            stop = start if row_slice.stop is None else row_slice.stop
            labels = self._constraint_labels(str(family), stop - start)
            for offset, position in enumerate(range(start, stop)):
                lhs = float(values[position])
                bound = float(bounds[position])
                slack = bound - lhs if kind == "inequality" else float("nan")
                residual = lhs - bound if kind == "equality" else 0.0
                binding = (
                    slack <= self.tolerance
                    if kind == "inequality"
                    else abs(residual) <= self.tolerance
                )
                marginal = (
                    float(marginals[position])
                    if marginals is not None and position < len(marginals)
                    else float("nan")
                )
                rows.append(
                    {
                        "kind": kind,
                        "family": str(family),
                        "label": labels[offset],
                        "realized_value": lhs,
                        "bound": bound,
                        "slack": slack,
                        "residual": residual,
                        "binding": binding,
                        "solver_marginal": marginal,
                        "improvement_per_unit": (
                            max(0.0, -marginal)
                            if kind == "inequality" and np.isfinite(marginal)
                            else float("nan")
                        ),
                    }
                )

    append_blocks(
        "inequality",
        self.problem.A_ub,
        self.problem.b_ub,
        self.problem.inequality_slices,
        self.diagnostics.inequality_marginals,
    )
    append_blocks(
        "equality",
        self.problem.A_eq,
        self.problem.b_eq,
        self.problem.equality_slices,
        self.diagnostics.equality_marginals,
    )
    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=CONSTRAINT_COLUMNS)

def bottlenecks(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return binding inequalities with a useful relaxation marginal."""
    constraints = self.constraints()
    selected = constraints[
        constraints["kind"].eq("inequality")
        & constraints["binding"].eq(True)
        & constraints["improvement_per_unit"].gt(self.tolerance)
    ].copy()
    order = np.lexsort(
        (
            np.asarray(selected["label"], dtype=str),
            np.asarray(selected["family"], dtype=str),
            -np.asarray(selected["improvement_per_unit"], dtype=np.float64),
        )
    )
    return selected.iloc[order].reset_index(drop=True)

def alternatives(self, good: str | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return scenario-allowed producer alternatives for one or all goods."""
    if good is not None and good not in self.goods_index:
        raise ValueError(f"Good '{good}' not found in goods index.")
    prices = self.state.market_prices
    rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    selected_rows = set(process_rows(self.realized_graph))
    goods = (
        (good,)
        if good is not None
        else good_keys(self.allowed_graph, self.goods_index)
    )
    for output_good in goods:
        good_id = good_node_id(output_good)
        if good_id not in self.allowed_graph:
            continue
        good_position = self.goods_index.index(output_good)
        for process_id in self.allowed_graph.predecessors(good_id):
            data = self.allowed_graph.nodes[process_id]
            if data.get("kind") != "process":
                continue
            i = int(data["row"])
            unit_input = float(self.problem.input_matrix[i] @ prices)
            unit_output = float(self.problem.output_matrix[i] @ prices)
            rows.append(
                {
                    "good": output_good,
                    "config": self.config_index[i],
                    "building": str(self.production.iloc[i]["building"]),
                    "production_method": str(
                        self.production.iloc[i]["production_method"]
                    ),
                    "era": int(self.production.iloc[i]["era"]),
                    "unit_output": float(
                        self.problem.output_matrix[i, good_position]
                    ),
                    "unit_input_cost": unit_input,
                    "unit_output_value": unit_output,
                    "unit_value_added": unit_output - unit_input,
                    "selected": i in selected_rows,
                    "level": float(self.state.building_levels[i]),
                    "parent_group": str(data.get("parent_group", "")),
                    "land_usage": str(data.get("land_usage", "")),
                    "is_extractive": bool(data.get("is_extractive", False)),
                    "is_subsistence": bool(data.get("is_subsistence", False)),
                    "discoverable_resource": bool(
                        data.get("discoverable_resource", False)
                    ),
                    "depletable_resource": bool(
                        data.get("depletable_resource", False)
                    ),
                }
            )
    frame = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=ALTERNATIVE_COLUMNS)
    if frame.empty:
        return frame
    frame = frame.sort_values("config", kind="mergesort")
    frame = frame.sort_values("unit_output", ascending=False, kind="mergesort")
    frame = frame.sort_values("selected", ascending=False, kind="mergesort")
    return frame.sort_values("good", kind="mergesort").reset_index(drop=True)

def summary(self) -> pd.Series:
    """Return headline, structural, and aggregate production-unit metrics.

    Chain fields include whole realized processes and their coproducts;
    system fields include all solved configurations. Resource columns use
    full extraction-building keys from the production snapshot, including
    unused types, and report levels and levels per 10,000 employed workers.
    Wage metrics require finite coefficients for contributing processes.
    Known zero denominators produce zero; unavailable wage data produce NaN.
    """
    terminal_position = self.goods_index.index(self.terminal_good)
    terminal_output = float(self.state.building_goods_output[terminal_position])
    terminal_net = float(
        self.state.building_levels @ self.problem.net_matrix[:, terminal_position]
    )
    chain = self.processes("realized")
    system_levels = self.state.building_levels
    system_gdp = self.state.gdp_weekly
    chain_gdp = float(np.asarray(chain["value_added"], dtype=np.float64).sum())
    system_employment = self.state.total_employment
    chain_employment = float(
        np.asarray(chain["employment"], dtype=np.float64).sum()
    )
    system_construction = float(system_levels @ self.construction_cost_vector)
    chain_construction = float(
        np.asarray(chain["construction_cost"], dtype=np.float64).sum()
    )
    system_land = float(system_levels @ self.arable_land_vector)
    chain_land = float(np.asarray(chain["arable_land"], dtype=np.float64).sum())
    system_infrastructure = float(system_levels @ self.infrastructure_vector)
    chain_infrastructure = float(
        np.asarray(chain["net_infrastructure_usage"], dtype=np.float64).sum()
    )
    realized_cycles = cyclic_nodes(self.realized_graph)
    realized_processes = self.processes("realized")
    allowed_processes = self.processes("allowed")
    values: dict[str, object] = {
        "scenario": self.scenario.display_name(),
        "terminal_good": self.terminal_good,
        "objective": self.scenario.objective,
        "solver_status": self.diagnostics.status,
        "solver_message": self.diagnostics.message,
        "objective_value": self.diagnostics.objective_value,
        "target_quantity": self.target_quantity,
        "target_base_value": self.target_quantity
        * float(self.state.market_prices[terminal_position]),
        "terminal_base_price": float(self.state.market_prices[terminal_position]),
        "terminal_gross_output": terminal_output,
        "terminal_net_output": terminal_net,
        "terminal_surplus": (
            terminal_net
            + float(self.state.imports[terminal_position])
            - float(self.state.exports[terminal_position])
            - (self.scenario.min_goods_balance or 0.0)
        ),
        "system_gdp_weekly": system_gdp,
        "system_gdp_annual": system_gdp * 52.0,
        "chain_gdp_weekly": chain_gdp,
        "chain_gdp_annual": chain_gdp * 52.0,
        "system_employment": system_employment,
        "chain_employment": chain_employment,
        "system_construction_cost": system_construction,
        "chain_construction_cost": chain_construction,
        "system_arable_land": system_land,
        "chain_arable_land": chain_land,
        "system_net_infrastructure_usage": system_infrastructure,
        "chain_net_infrastructure_usage": chain_infrastructure,
        "employment_per_terminal_unit": _safe_divide(
            chain_employment, terminal_net
        ),
        "construction_per_terminal_unit": _safe_divide(
            chain_construction, terminal_net
        ),
        "gdp_per_terminal_unit": _safe_divide(chain_gdp, terminal_net),
        "output_per_10k_workers": _safe_divide(
            terminal_net * 10_000.0, chain_employment
        ),
        "realized_process_count": len(realized_processes),
        "realized_good_count": sum(
            data.get("kind") == "good"
            for _node, data in self.realized_graph.nodes(data=True)
        ),
        "realized_edge_count": self.realized_graph.number_of_edges(),
        "allowed_process_count": len(allowed_processes),
        "allowed_good_count": sum(
            data.get("kind") == "good"
            for _node, data in self.allowed_graph.nodes(data=True)
        ),
        "allowed_edge_count": self.allowed_graph.number_of_edges(),
        "cyclic_component_count": cyclic_component_count(self.realized_graph),
        "cyclic_node_count": len(realized_cycles),
        "condensation_depth": condensation_depth(self.realized_graph),
        "extractive_process_count": int(
            np.asarray(realized_processes["is_extractive"], dtype=bool).sum()
        ),
        "resource_process_count": int(
            (
                np.asarray(realized_processes["discoverable_resource"], dtype=bool)
                | np.asarray(realized_processes["depletable_resource"], dtype=bool)
            ).sum()
        ),
        "chain_gdp_share": _safe_divide(chain_gdp, system_gdp),
        "chain_employment_share": _safe_divide(chain_employment, system_employment),
        "chain_construction_share": _safe_divide(
            chain_construction, system_construction
        ),
        "chain_arable_land_share": _safe_divide(chain_land, system_land),
        "chain_infrastructure_share": _safe_divide(
            chain_infrastructure, system_infrastructure
        ),
    }
    chain_levels = np.zeros_like(system_levels)
    chain_rows = list(self._rows_for_view("realized"))
    chain_levels[chain_rows] = system_levels[chain_rows]
    building_keys = self.production["building"].astype(str).to_numpy()
    buildings = resource_buildings(self.production)
    for scope, levels, gdp, employment, construction in (
        (
            "system",
            system_levels,
            system_gdp,
            system_employment,
            system_construction,
        ),
        ("chain", chain_levels, chain_gdp, chain_employment, chain_construction),
    ):
        wage_employment = float("nan")
        if "wage_normalized_employment" in self.production.columns:
            contributing = levels != 0.0
            coefficients = self.production["wage_normalized_employment"].to_numpy(
                dtype=np.float64, na_value=np.nan
            )[contributing]
            if np.isfinite(coefficients).all():
                wage_employment = float(levels[contributing] @ coefficients)
        values[f"{scope}_wage_normalized_employment"] = wage_employment
        for metric, denominator in (
            ("gdp_per_capita", employment / self.state.workforce_ratio),
            ("gdp_per_wage_normalized_employment", wage_employment),
            ("gdp_per_construction_cost", construction),
        ):
            weekly = _safe_divide(gdp, denominator)
            values[f"{scope}_{metric}_weekly"] = weekly
            values[f"{scope}_{metric}_annual"] = weekly * 52.0
        for building in buildings:
            building_levels = float(levels[building_keys == building].sum())
            values[f"{scope}_levels_{building}"] = building_levels
            values[f"{scope}_levels_per_10k_pop_{building}"] = _safe_divide(
                building_levels * 10_000.0, employment
            )
    return pd.Series(
        values,
        index=[*SUMMARY_FIELDS, *resource_level_fields(self.production)],
        name=self.terminal_good,
    )

Analyze goods with at least the requested base-price export value.

Each terminal export amount is the higher of its aggregated template exports and target_value / base_price. Other exports and all imports are retained. Target metadata reports the effective terminal exports.

Summary columns include fixed economic metrics and per-building resource levels derived from the full economy, including banned and unused types. def sweep_supply_chains(
    economy: Economy,
    scenario_template: Scenario,
    *,
    goods: Iterable[str] | None = None,
    target_value: float = 100_000.0,
    keep_results: bool = False,
    tolerance: float = 1e-9,
) -> SupplyChainSweepResult:
    """Analyze goods with at least the requested base-price export value.

    Each terminal export amount is the higher of its aggregated template
    exports and ``target_value / base_price``. Other exports and all imports
    are retained. Target metadata reports the effective terminal exports.

    Summary columns include fixed economic metrics and per-building resource
    levels derived from the full economy, including banned and unused types.
    Empty sweeps retain the same columns; failed solves use NaN for metrics.
    ``df_building_levels`` retains every production unit's solved level for
    each requested good, independently of ``keep_results``; failures use NaN.
    """
    if not np.isfinite(target_value) or target_value <= 0:
        raise ValueError("target_value must be a positive finite number.")
    selected_goods = list(economy.producible_goods) if goods is None else list(goods)
    if len(selected_goods) != len(set(selected_goods)):
        raise ValueError("goods must not contain duplicates.")
    goods_index = economy.goods_index
    unknown = [good for good in selected_goods if good not in goods_index]
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(f"Goods not found in goods index: {unknown}")

    template_exports = goods_order_vector(
        goods_index, scenario_template.goods_export, "goods_export"
    )
    prices = dict(zip(goods_index, economy.base_prices))
    columns = sweep_columns(economy.df_production)
    rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    retained: dict[str, SupplyChainResult] = {}
    building_levels = pd.DataFrame(
        np.nan,
        index=pd.Index(economy.building_index, name="config"),
        columns=selected_goods,
        dtype=np.float64,
    )
    for good in selected_goods:
        price = float(prices[good])
        if not np.isfinite(price) or price <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"Good '{good}' must have a positive finite base price.")
        amount = max(
            float(template_exports[goods_index.index(good)]),
            float(target_value / price),
        )
        name = (
            f"{scenario_template.name}:{good}"
            if scenario_template.name is not None
            else good
        )
        scenario = replace(
            scenario_template,
            goods_export=tuple(
                (key, value)
                for key, value in scenario_template.goods_export
                if key != good
            )
            + ((good, amount),),
            name=name,
        )
        try:
            result = SupplyChainAnalyzer(
                economy,
                scenario,
                good,
                tolerance=tolerance,
            ).run()
            row: dict[str, object] = {
                str(key): value for key, value in result.summary().items()
            }
            row.update(
                {
                    "good": good,
                    "status": "success",
                    "error_type": "",
                    "error_message": "",
                }
            )
            building_levels[good] = result.state.building_levels
            if keep_results:
                retained[good] = result
        except ValueError as exc:
            row = {field: float("nan") for field in columns}
            row.update(
                {
                    "good": good,
                    "status": "failure",
                    "error_type": type(exc).__name__,
                    "error_message": str(exc),
                    "scenario": name,
                    "terminal_good": good,
                    "objective": scenario.objective,
                    "solver_status": -1,
                    "solver_message": str(exc),
                    "target_quantity": amount,
                    "target_base_value": amount * price,
                    "terminal_base_price": price,
                }
            )
        rows.append(row)

    summary = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=columns)
    failures = pd.DataFrame(
        summary.loc[summary["status"].eq("failure"), :]
    ).reset_index(drop=True)
    return SupplyChainSweepResult(
        _summary=summary,
        _failures=failures,
        _building_levels=building_levels,
        _results=retained,
    )

docs.title: Data dictionary
docs.text:
This reference covers columns deliberately created, selected, or transformed by the package. It applies to public DataFrame reports and example exports:

  • Parser outputs: identifiers, normalized fields, and generated families.
  • Production configurations: the analytical production table.
  • Economy reports: solved building, market, and population tables and the Japan comparison.
  • Supply-chain reports: summary, detailed reports, sweeps, and example additions.

Arbitrary game-defined attributes copied through unchanged, such as icon in buildings.csv, are outside this dictionary. A patch or mod can introduce such fields without changing the parser. The parser page describes their general representation and the transformations applied to them. Dynamic names with a known meaning are documented once per family, such as goods_<good>; replace the placeholder with the actual script key, for example goods_steel.

docs.title: Shared conventions
docs.text: Convention Interpretation Script identifiers Strings such as building_steel_mills, steel, and pm_bessemer_process; use these for joins. Display translations are separate columns. Configuration identifiers Economy.building_index joins building and the complete production_method string with +. A configuration represents one combination of production methods, not all levels of a building type. Compound strings Many parser lists and production-method combinations use + as a separator. The parser keeps source order; these strings are not localized unless a separate localization column is requested. Numeric types “Number” means integer or floating point as appropriate to source data; solved levels and totals can be fractional because optimization is continuous. CSV has no stored dtype; pandas inference can change with missing values. Goods quantities Weekly goods units or orders, rather than physical SI units. Per-level coefficients describe a fully staffed level; solved totals multiply coefficients by levels and applicable throughput multipliers. Money Game currency (£). Nominal values use goods cost as base price; market values use the state's national prices. Output minus input value excludes payroll and other costs absent from the model. Annualization Annual GDP is weekly GDP multiplied by 52. Employment, building levels, construction points, land, prices, and dimensionless ratios are not annualized. Construction Construction points required to build the modeled levels, not a weekly expense or elapsed construction time. Population / per capita Employment counts workers; total population and GDP per capita include dependents inferred from workforce_ratio. The default 1.0 preserves worker-only values. Unemployed workers are not inferred. Historical snapshots used worker-only denominators. Fractions and percentages Shares and margins use fractions, so 0.2 means 20%. The economy market report's market_prices_variance instead uses percent units (20 means +20%). Signed infrastructure shares need not lie between zero and one. Infrastructure Positive net usage consumes infrastructure; negative net usage provides it. Zero can mean no footprint or exactly offset consumption and provision. Missing values pd.NA / NaN mean missing or undefined; CSV generally writes them as blank cells. Empty strings also become blank CSV cells and may be read back as NaN. See each table for defaults. Division Production profit ratios use ordinary division: nonzero divided by zero gives signed infinity, and zero divided by zero gives NaN. Supply-chain safe ratios return 0.0 when the denominator is exactly zero; they do not clamp negative denominators. Stable schemas Supply-chain reports retain their named columns even when empty. Generic parser columns depend on the game data; optional enrichments can add or omit columns.

docs.title: Model and source boundaries
docs.text:
The production table aggregates the selected methods' signed goods flows. Economy splits those net coefficients into nonnegative input and output matrices. They are often described as gross input/output matrices in the API, but opposing flows already canceled in a production row cannot be recovered. Profit and GDP measure the modeled goods-value difference, not accounting profit after wages. A process producing multiple goods retains its entire output value; the supply-chain API does not allocate its employment or value added to one coproduct.

Nominal supply-chain optimization uses fixed prices and fixed throughput, without economy-of-scale bonuses. Market solving changes national prices but does not simulate shortages, local prices/MAPI, endogenous population demand, or wealth feedback. Population report wealth starts from the pop-types table; it is not a solved household-income distribution.

Column definitions follow the current source calculations, not a promise that old CSV snapshots match every optional field. See the parsing guide for game-version and localization behavior and the API reference for call signatures.

docs.title: Economy reports
docs.text: These reports export a supplied EconomyState; they do not solve a new scenario. Totals include the entire modeled economy. Monetary values use its state prices, which are base prices in nominal mode and national market prices in market and equilibrium modes. See shared conventions.

docs.title: Snapshot ownership
docs.text:
EconomyState composes context: EconomyContext, market: MarketState, and households: PopState. Flat reads forward to these components. Market and complete state reference the exact same context object; replacing only market or household results shares the fixed arrays.

Owner Stored quantities Derived quantities EconomyContext Building levels, realized flows, gross imports and exports, worker counts, workforce ratio Net trade, input/output totals, sell orders, industrial/export orders, population totals MarketState Shared context and prices Building surplus/deficit, GDP PopState Wealth, demand, optional weekly income/expenses Weekly balance (income - expenses), or None when either is absent EconomyState Component references, optional equilibrium diagnostics Total buy orders, wealth summaries, per-capita reports

EconomyState.pop_buy_orders forwards to the read-only, goods-aligned PopState.pop_buy_orders array of weekly household demand. Total buy_orders adds these population orders to non_pop_buy_orders.

Prepared context fields default to None: goods_buy_packages is an immutable GoodsBuyPackages object whose read-only quantities array is wealth-by-goods float64 in goods_index column order, and whose read-only wealth array contains ascending positive int64 wealth labels; consumption_scales is read-only float64, shaped like worker counts. prepare_context() fills missing fields explicitly. Nominal/market solving leaves these and household finances unevaluated. Economy.df_buy_packages continues to hold raw category budgets, distinct from prepared goods quantities.

goods_buy_packages() returns the same GoodsBuyPackages representation, reusing prepared baskets when available. df_goods_buy_packages(source) exports a state, context, or basket object as an independent DataFrame: an ascending int64 index named wealth, and float64 goods-quantity columns in goods_index order.

docs.title: Building registry
docs.text:
Economy.df_buildings(state) returns one row per configuration with level strictly greater than zero, sorted by level descending. It does not aggregate different configurations of the same building type. The returned DataFrame is independent and mutable; editing it does not change the economy or state.

Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases building String / building key Building key from the aligned production-table row. Replaces the building portion of the former combined key column. production_method String / PM combination Complete production-method combination from the aligned production-table row. Multiple PM keys remain joined by +; configurations are not aggregated. level Float / building levels Solved level for that configuration. Fractional levels are allowed; zero/negative levels are filtered out. construction_cost Float / construction points Per-level construction coefficient times level. Zero-cost configurations can have positive levels. building_surplus Float / £ per week state.building_surplus: realized goods value added before wages at state prices. Negative values are retained. profit_per_capita Float / £ per worker per week building_surplus / employment. Excludes dependents regardless of workforce_ratio; NaN for zero employment. employment Float / workers Row sum of state.pops. Realized total across all professions. goods_<good> Float / units per week Aligned column of state.building_goods_flow. Positive outputs, negative inputs; already includes levels and throughput. employment_<profession> Float / workers Aligned column of state.pops. Already includes building levels; excludes dependents.

Columns follow the order above, with all goods_<good> columns in Economy.goods_index order, then all employment_<profession> columns in Economy.pop_index order. Entirely zero columns are retained, including when the report has no rows. Building and PM columns use game keys rather than localized names; the former combined key column is removed.

docs.title: Historical building registry
docs.text:
The committed artifacts/analyses/optimization/equilibrium/buildings.csv uses the earlier three-column schema: key, level, and construction_cost. Level and construction cost retain the meanings above. New exports use the expanded building registry schema.

Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases key String / configuration identifier building + "+" + production_method from Economy.building_index. Historical snapshot only; current reports provide separate building and PM columns.

docs.title: State flows and cooperative income
docs.text:
EconomyContext.goods_import and goods_export are read-only float64 vectors aligned to goods_index, holding non-negative weekly gross trade quantities. A good may have both import and export orders. EconomyState forwards both arrays; imports and exports alias the respective arrays on context and state. The cached read-only goods_trade_flow vector is goods_import - goods_export. Market orders use the gross quantities independently.

EconomyState.building_goods_flow is a read-only float64 matrix with rows aligned to building_index and columns to goods_index. Values are realized weekly signed quantities after building levels, throughput, and economy of scale: positive for outputs and negative for inputs. Aggregate input/output attributes are derived from this matrix. The flow matrix is owned by EconomyContext; aggregate inputs/outputs are cached there, while financial aggregates are cached on MarketState.

Attribute / result Shape / unit Meaning / calculation building_goods_input Goods / units per week maximum(-building_goods_flow, 0).sum(axis=0). building_goods_output Goods / units per week maximum(building_goods_flow, 0).sum(axis=0). building_surplus Configurations / £ per week building_goods_flow @ market_prices, value added before wages; may be negative. building_deficit Configurations / £ per week maximum(-building_surplus, 0), operating losses before subsidies. pop_income(state) Configurations × professions / £ per week Positive surplus allocated by pops * wage_weight, plus pops * dependents_per_worker * dependent_wage / 52; household totals, not per-worker rates.

The four state properties are cached, owned, read-only float64 arrays. Signs are split before aggregation to retain opposing flows between configurations; within-row flows retain the production table's signed-net convention.

The income calculation returns a fresh writable matrix. It includes professions regardless of paid_private_wage, pays zero wages on zero/negative surplus, and does not pool configurations. Positive surplus with zero total recipient weight raises ValueError. With subsidies disabled, deficits have no funding source. Dependent earnings are exogenous and do not alter building surplus or production GDP. Missing dependent wages mean zero. Income excludes transfers, reserves, and subsistence income, and is untaxed unless operating-loss subsidies are enabled; it does not update pop_balance or wealth.

docs.title: Household consumption calculations
docs.text:
Let s_ij = pops_ij / 10_000 * consumption_mult_j * (1 + 0.5 * dependents_per_worker) and Q_wg be the quantities matrix from goods_buy_packages(state).

Result Shape / unit Meaning / calculation pop_consumption_scales(state) Configurations × professions / dimensionless s_ij, multiples of a weekly basket for 10,000 standard workers. Missing profession multipliers default to one. pop_buy_orders(state, ...) Goods / units per week sum_ij(s_ij * Q[pop_wealth_ij, g]). pop_expenses(state, ...) Configurations × professions / £ per week s_ij * sum_g(Q[pop_wealth_ij, g] * market_prices_g), household totals.

All three return independent writable float64 arrays. Needs and expenses accept optional goods_buy_packages: GoodsBuyPackages | None and consumption_scales, independently. Each resolves explicit arguments first, then prepared context values, then calculation. Supplied scales are authoritative and already include all population factors; they must match the population shape, be finite and nonnegative, and be zero for empty cells. Unused profession multipliers are not validated when scales are supplied. Occupied cells require a basket even when their scale is zero; empty cells have zero expenses and need no defined wealth tier.

Scales can be reused while population assumptions are fixed; baskets can be reused while production, trade, and substitution assumptions are fixed. Both allow wealth and market prices to change. Supplied baskets skip validation of unused goods flows, base prices, and raw need/package definitions. Expenses use finite nonnegative market prices, including zero. Non-finite calculated results are errors.

Total expenses equal population demand valued at market prices when using the same inputs. These helpers do not update the state; compute weekly balances as pop_income(state) - pop_expenses(state). Expenses exclude taxes, rationing, affordability restrictions, and wealth transitions.

docs.title: Equilibrium diagnostics
docs.text:
EconomyState.equilibrium_diagnostics is None for nominal/market solves and manually composed snapshots unless explicitly supplied. Equilibrium successes and EquilibriumError.state carry immutable EquilibriumDiagnostics. error.diagnostics is the same object as on its retained state. All demand, prices, wealth, income, expenses, and balances in that state describe the same evaluation. Runtime calculation errors retain the preceding complete evaluation and chain the original error.

Field Type / unit Meaning status String converged, cycle, max_iterations, evaluation_failed, verification_failed, or insufficient_income. iterations Integer / transition steps Completed transitions after initialization; excludes final verification. Initially stable wealth reports zero. increasing_cells Tuple of integer pairs Occupied configuration/profession coordinates requiring a permitted increase. decreasing_cells Tuple of integer pairs Occupied configuration/profession coordinates requiring a permitted decrease. unaffordable_floor_cells Tuple of integer pairs Occupied minimum-tier households below the lower affordability threshold; downward changes are blocked. loss_buildings Tuple of integers Configuration indices with unfunded losses exceeding atol + rtol * max(output_value, input_value); empty when all operating losses are subsidized. cycle_start Integer or None / iteration index First appearance of the repeated wealth assignment, counting initialization as zero. cycle_length Integer or None / transition steps Detected cycle period; only populated with cycle_start for cycles.

Coordinates use Economy.building_index and Economy.pop_index in row-major order. Loss values follow the current signed-net production-flow convention and use weekly pounds; household affordability uses weekly group totals. converged means no permitted wealth changes remain, including at boundaries. It does not guarantee affordability or self-financing buildings: the two financial flags do not change success status. Setup and initial-evaluation errors other than insufficient income raise ValueError without a partial result.

Equilibrium solves, optimizers, and direct contexts default to subsidize_operating_losses=True; pass False to disable the policy. Nominal and market solves default to disabled. With the policy enabled, pop_income is disposable income after the uniform tax funding all operating losses. The optional pop_income_tax matrix stores weekly household taxes, and pop_income_before_tax derives gross income as income plus tax. All three follow configuration × profession order; the tax includes dependent earnings. Evaluated untaxed snapshots store zero taxes; unevaluated snapshots use None. The context retains the policy flag. Economy.pop_income_tax(state) recalculates taxes without modifying the state.

An insufficient_income error occurs when losses exceed total gross income. Unlike other initial evaluation errors, it carries the failing snapshot even at initialization. This unsuccessful snapshot records pre-tax income and zero tax collected. Its iteration count identifies the failing wealth assignment.

docs.title: Market report
docs.text:
Economy.df_market(state) returns one row per good with positive sell or buy orders, sorted by sell orders descending. Goods quantities are weekly; they include throughput effects already applied to the state. “Gross” input and output totals are reconstructed from production-table net coefficients.

Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases goods String / identifier Good key aligned with Economy.goods_index. Includes only goods surviving the order filter. market_prices Float / £ per goods unit Price in the supplied state. Base price in nominal mode; market mode derives it from buy/sell orders. market_prices_variance Float / percent price change 100 * (market_prices / base_prices - 1). 20 means +20%; not statistical variance. Ordinary division at zero base price. sell_orders Float / goods units per week building_goods_output + imports. Zero is valid when only buy orders are positive. buy_orders Float / goods units per week building_goods_input + exports + pop_needs. Zero is valid when only sell orders are positive. building_goods_input Float / goods units per week Sum of configuration levels times adjusted nonnegative input coefficients. Positive consumption magnitude, unlike signed production-table goods columns. building_goods_output Float / goods units per week Sum of configuration levels times adjusted nonnegative output coefficients. Positive production magnitude. imports Float / goods units per week The good's state.goods_import quantity. Non-negative; may coexist with exports. exports Float / goods units per week The good's state.goods_export quantity. Non-negative; may coexist with imports. pop_needs Float / goods units per week Population-demand orders from state.pop_buy_orders. Zero in nominal/market solves; calculated from wealth baskets by household evaluation and equilibrium solving.

docs.title: Population report
docs.text:
Economy.df_pop(state) returns one row per profession with positive employment, sorted by employment descending and with its index reset. Let n_ij be workers of profession j in configuration i, and w_ij their stored wealth level. Let r = state.workforce_ratio and d = state.dependents_per_worker = (1-r)/r. total_employment sums workers; total_population divides that sum by r. Both direct contexts and solve() default to r=1.0.

Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases profession String / identifier Profession key aligned with Economy.pop_index. Zero-employment professions are omitted. employment Float / workers sum_i(n_ij). Includes the whole system, not just one terminal chain. employment_share Float / fraction Profession employment divided by all modeled employment. State returns zeros for zero total employment; such a report has no positive-employment rows. dependents Float / people sum_i(n_ij) * d. Derived using the same economy-wide ratio for every profession. population Float / people sum_i(n_ij) / r. Workers plus dependents. avg_wealth Float / wealth level sum_i(w_ij * n_ij) / sum_i(n_ij). State returns zero for a profession without employment. Nominal/market modes use starting tiers; equilibrium mode iterates them. total_wealth Float / population-weighted wealth levels sum_i(w_ij * n_ij) / r. Dependents share household wealth; not a stock of money or GDP. pop_balance Float / £ per week Sum of derived household income minus expenses over configurations for this profession. NaN until both income and expenses are supplied on PopState; nominal and market solves leave them as None.

state.average_wealth_by_profession contains profession averages, while state.total_wealth_by_profession caches employment-weighted wealth sums, excluding dependents. The report divides those sums by the workforce ratio for its population-weighted total_wealth column. Because dependents share household wealth and the workforce ratio is uniform, state.average_wealth equals total wealth divided by total population and supplies state.wealth_distribution["mean"]. Both return zero for an empty population.

docs.title: Equilibrium optimization summary
docs.text:
examples/optimize_equilibrium.py writes one row per completed local search to artifacts/analyses/optimization/equilibrium/summary.csv, including the worse attempt that ends iteration. The current objective is average wealth. A resumed invocation includes iteration zero for the re-evaluated saved solution, with empty search diagnostics. is_best identifies the earliest highest-objective state exported in the solution files. Each local search gets a fresh trial budget; equal objectives continue until a strict decrease or the optional iteration cap. A budget-limited search may return a verified state with an unsuccessful search status. Validation and equilibrium errors propagate without writing new files. The companion buildings.csv uses the building registry schema above.

Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases objective String / category Scenario objective, currently average_wealth. Older snapshots may use gdp; GDP remains a reported metric. employment_cap Integer / workers Upper bound on employed workers, 1,000,000. Does not require full employment. workforce_ratio Float / fraction Workers divided by total population, 0.4. Shared uniformly across households. subsidize_operating_losses Boolean Whether a uniform household income tax funds operating losses. Defaults to true; applies to every equilibrium evaluation, including saved baselines and restarts. banned_building_groups String / identifiers Semicolon-separated DEFAULT_BANNED_BGS. Excluded configurations have zero levels. min_net_infrastructure Float or empty / infrastructure units Scenario minimum infrastructure generation minus consumption. Empty in both equilibrium examples: infrastructure is unconstrained. If configured elsewhere, zero prevents deficits; positive values require surplus; negative values allow a bounded deficit. min_net_infrastructure_usage Float / infrastructure units Historical minimum consumption minus generation. Present only in older snapshots. Replaced by min_net_infrastructure, which uses the opposite sign convention; the old name is no longer a scenario parameter. min_goods_balance Float or empty / weekly goods units Minimum building output + imports − building inputs − exports, for every good. Excludes household consumption; empty means None, disabling the floor. throughput_multiplier Float / multiplier Common fixed multiplier, 1.0. No throughput bonus. economy_of_scale_level_cap Float / building levels Economy-of-scale cap, zero. Level-dependent bonuses are disabled. configuration_count Integer / configurations Number of configurations in the selected production basis. Includes configurations with zero returned levels. construction_cost Float / construction points Model construction cost at this row's returned levels. Uses the current production coefficients. arable_land_consumption Float / land units Model arable-land consumption at this row's returned levels. No arable-land cap is added by this example. max_evaluations Integer / trials Requested hard budget for each local search. Separate starting-point/baseline evaluations and final verification are additional solves. initial_equilibrium_status String / category converged or insufficient_income for the starting mix. An unfunded start is passed to the optimizer without accepting it as a valid baseline. initial_gdp_weekly Float / £ per week GDP at this search's initial mix after household equilibrium. Empty for an unfunded start, as are initial annual GDP and average wealth. Uses the same scenario and wealth seed as search trials; baseline rows use their own state. initial_annual_gdp Float / £ per year 52 * initial_gdp_weekly. Baseline for comparison with the final state. gdp_weekly Float / £ per week This row's returned equilibrium GDP. Selection uses the scenario objective, which may differ from GDP. annual_gdp Float / £ per year 52 * gdp_weekly. Includes all modeled production. employment Float / workers Returned state's total employed workers. At most the cap within solver tolerance. population Float / people employment / workforce_ratio. Includes dependents. gdp_per_capita Float / £ per person per year Annual GDP divided by total population. Zero for an empty population. average_wealth Float / wealth tier Population-weighted household wealth tier. Equal to employment-weighted wealth with a uniform workforce ratio. net_infrastructure_usage Float / infrastructure units Consumption minus generation: levels dotted with the model infrastructure vector. Diagnostic in both equilibrium examples; positive values are permitted. When a minimum is configured elsewhere, at most -min_net_infrastructure within solver tolerance. search_success Boolean Optimizer search success flag. Can be false for a saved, converged household equilibrium. search_status Integer / code Optimizer termination code. Interpret together with search_message. search_message String / diagnostic text Search termination message. Explicitly reports budget exhaustion. trial_evaluations Integer / trials Optimizer result.nfev. Includes rejected physical trials; consecutive repeated points reuse a score. equilibrium_evaluations Integer / inner attempts Household solves attempted by the search. Excludes the separate baseline and final verification. failed_equilibrium_evaluations Integer / inner failures Sum of trial equilibrium failures across diagnostic statuses. Failed trials are skipped while search continues. equilibrium_status String / category Household solver status for the returned state. Always converged in a saved result. equilibrium_iterations Integer / transitions Household transition steps in the fresh final solve. Initialization and final accounting verification are excluded. loss_buildings_count Integer / configurations Number of materially loss-making configurations. A financial flag, without implicit financing. unaffordable_floor_cells_count Integer / household cells Number of configuration/profession cells unable to afford the lowest tier. A financial flag that does not prevent numerical convergence. iteration Integer / searches One-based local-search number. Zero identifies the re-evaluated saved baseline on resume. initialization String / category equal_configurations, saved_solution, or previous_iteration. The fresh initial mix scales equal allowed configuration levels to the employment cap without balancing infrastructure. initial_average_wealth Float / wealth tier Average wealth at this search's starting levels. Baseline rows use their own state. loss_reduction Float / fraction Fraction applied to loss-making configurations before this search. Defaults to 0.5; zero for a fresh first search or baseline row. reduced_configuration_count Integer / configurations Number of levels actually reduced before this search. No employment rescaling is applied. objective_value Float / objective units Returned objective in the optimizer's units, currently average wealth. GDP-based objectives, if configured, use weekly units. objective_change Float / objective units Objective minus the preceding search's value, or saved baseline for a first resumed search. Empty without a predecessor; a strict negative value ends iteration. gdp_weekly_change Float / £ per week GDP minus the preceding search's GDP, or saved baseline on first resume. Diagnostic only when maximizing wealth; empty without a predecessor. started_at_utc String / ISO timestamp UTC start time for this search. Baseline rows record invocation setup start. elapsed_seconds Float / seconds Search duration including starting-point evaluation. Baseline rows cover setup through saved-state evaluation and adjustment. is_best Boolean True only for the earliest highest-objective row. All solution reports use that row's state. completed_iterations Integer / searches Total completed local searches in the invocation. Excludes the saved baseline; repeated on all rows. total_trial_evaluations Integer / trials Sum of local-search trial counts. Excludes separate baseline/starting evaluations and final verification; repeated on all rows. total_elapsed_seconds Float / seconds Invocation elapsed time through summary preparation. Excludes CSV writes; repeated on all rows. best_iteration Integer / searches Selected best row's iteration number. Zero when the saved baseline wins; repeated on all rows. max_iterations Integer or empty / searches Optional cap on completed local searches. Empty means unlimited. stop_reason String / category objective_worsened or max_iterations. A strict decrease takes precedence if both conditions apply.

docs.title: Japan optimization comparison
docs.text:
The current examples/optimize_jap.py writes optimize_jap.csv, one row per employment-cap scenario, in increasing cap order. It solves a nominal autarkic era-5 economy with selected Japanese state-region resource and arable-land limits and the example's banned building groups. Its employment and other totals are whole-system values.

Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases employment_cap Integer / workers Scenario upper bound on total modeled employment. Retained on both success and failure; not the realized employment. status String / category success or failure for the solve. Failure records a caught ValueError. annual_gdp Float / £ per year 52 * state.gdp_weekly, using base prices in this example. NaN on failure. employment Float / workers Sum of the state's employment array. NaN on failure. construction_cost Float / construction points Solved levels dotted with per-level construction coefficients. NaN on failure. gdp_per_capita Float / £ per worker per year Annual GDP divided by modeled employment. Zero for zero employment on a successful state; NaN on failure. arable_land_consumption Float / arable-land units Solved levels dotted with the model's arable-land coefficients. NaN on failure. Recognized agricultural building groups consume one unit per level; others zero. error String / diagnostic text Caught exception message. Empty string on success; no economic metric is inferred from a failure.

docs.title: Additional columns in the committed snapshot
docs.text:
The committed artifacts/analyses/optimization/japan/employment_sweep.csv was generated by an earlier version of the example (the generator at commit 7e3365c used compare_scenarios). It has no status column: an empty error indicates success. Shared metrics have the meanings above, except the earlier per-capita calculation returned infinity when successful employment was zero. These additional columns are still documented for readers of that snapshot; the current generator does not emit them.

Column or family Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases objective String / category Scenario objective, gdp in the Japan snapshot. Snapshot-only; retained on failure. gdp_per_construction Float / £ per year per construction point Annual GDP divided by solved construction cost. Snapshot-only; zero for nonpositive construction cost, NaN on failure. era_cap Integer or None / era limit Scenario's maximum allowed technology era, 5 in this snapshot. Snapshot-only; retained on failure. level_<building> Float / building levels Sum of solved levels across configurations of a resource-limited building type; e.g. level_building_coal_mine. Snapshot-only family in first-seen building order; zero if unbuilt, NaN on failure.

The recognized groups are bg_staple_crops, bg_ranching, bg_agriculture, bg_plantations, bg_subsistence_agriculture, and bg_subsistence_ranching. The coefficient uses immediate building_group membership, not land_usage or ancestor traversal; a missing group column gives all-zero coefficients.

These legacy fields were traced to the earlier comparison implementation; their presence does not imply that the current example and stored snapshot share the same output schema.

For the report APIs, see the economy API. The resource-limited optimization showcase describes the Japan experiment.

docs.title: Supply-chain equilibrium exports
docs.text:
The separate examples/optimize_supply_chain_equilibrium.py example exports:

Its input recipes come from era_5_automation/building_levels.csv, exported by the supply-chain comparison example. Rows are aligned to the full production table before units unused by all selected recipes are removed. Each retained coefficient is used without normalization. The example trusts the saved input and selects its hard-coded ALLOWED_CHAIN_GOODS without reading the adjacent summary.csv. Target metadata assumes £100,000 per recipe and derives target quantities from goods base prices. Chain metadata follows the optimizer's column order.

File / column Meaning chain_matrix.csv: config Building plus production-method key; rows follow the selected production table. chain_matrix.csv: terminal-good columns Building-level coefficients for one saved chain recipe. Columns follow the example's ALLOWED_CHAIN_GOODS order. chains.csv: good Terminal good identifying a matrix column. chains.csv: target_quantity Weekly terminal export orders used to generate one recipe. Imports and coproducts affect the required domestic output. chains.csv: target_base_value Terminal target quantity times base price; £100,000 per saved recipe. chains.csv: initial_level Starting multiplier of the saved recipe for the invocation, after any resume reduction. chains.csv: level Best verified chain multiplier across local searches and the eligible saved baseline. chains.csv: previous_level Saved chain multiplier before reducing losses; present on resumed runs. chains.csv: previous_terminal_surplus Recipe-attributed weekly operating surplus of terminal-good producers at the re-evaluated saved solution, including coproduct revenue; present on resumed runs. summary.csv: recipe_configuration Source collection, era_5_automation. summary.csv: chain_count Number of chain decision variables. summary.csv: configuration_count Number of building-configuration rows in the basis. summary.csv: iteration One-based local-search number; zero identifies the re-evaluated saved baseline on resumed invocations. summary.csv: initial_average_wealth, initial_gdp_weekly, initial_annual_gdp Metrics at that local search's starting vector; baseline rows use their own state. summary.csv: initialization equal_chains for a fresh first search, saved_solution for a resume baseline/first search, or previous_iteration for subsequent searches. summary.csv: loss_reduction Fraction applied to loss-making chains before this search. Equal-chain initialization and baseline rows record zero. summary.csv: reduced_chain_count Number of chain levels actually reduced before this search. summary.csv: max_evaluations Hard trial budget for each local search. summary.csv: gdp_weekly_change Returned weekly GDP minus the preceding search's GDP, or the saved baseline's GDP for the first resumed search; empty without a predecessor. summary.csv: started_at_utc, elapsed_seconds UTC ISO timestamp and elapsed seconds for this search including its starting-point evaluation; baseline rows describe invocation setup through saved-state evaluation and adjustment. summary.csv: is_best True only for the earliest highest-GDP row, whose state is exported in the solution reports. summary.csv: completed_iterations Total completed local searches, excluding the saved baseline; repeated on every row. summary.csv: total_trial_evaluations Sum of local-search trial counts, excluding separate baseline/starting evaluations and final verification; repeated on every row. summary.csv: total_elapsed_seconds Invocation elapsed seconds through summary preparation, excluding CSV writes; repeated on every row. summary.csv: best_iteration Selected best row's iteration number, including zero when the saved baseline wins; repeated on every row. summary.csv: max_iterations Optional cap on completed local searches; empty means unlimited. summary.csv: stop_reason objective_worsened for a strict decrease from the preceding result, otherwise max_iterations when the configured cap is reached; repeated on every row.

Each summary row describes its own returned state, including the worse search that triggers stopping. Equal GDP continues iteration; ties select the earliest best state. Baseline rows have empty search diagnostics, retaining their current economic and household-equilibrium metrics. Other summary columns follow the equilibrium optimization summary. buildings.csv follows the building registry, including only positive building levels and sorting by level. Reconstruct those levels by multiplying the labeled matrix by chains.csv's level column, then align by building + "+" + production_method.

market.csv, pop.csv, and goods_buy_packages.csv use the same full report exports as examples/optimize_equilibrium.py: Economy.df_market(state), Economy.df_pop(state), and Economy.df_goods_buy_packages(state) with the wealth index reset to a CSV column.

docs.title: Parser outputs
docs.text: These entries describe package-defined columns. Other attributes, such as an icon path or an AI weight, are passed through from the game and are not an enumerated schema. Values and concrete family members depend on game version and mods. See shared conventions.

docs.title: Identifiers and localization
docs.text:
Buildings, building groups, goods, population types, state regions, and technologies normally have one row per script definition, identified by key. Population needs instead have one row per need/good entry, so key repeats. Production-method rows use the three identifiers described below. Buy packages use numeric wealth.

Column Type / unit Meaning / source Presence / edge cases key String / identifier Definition key from its source file; in population needs, the need key rather than a unique row key. Included by these parsers, even when other attributes vary. key_localization Nullable string / display text Lookup of key in the requested language. Only with language; missing lookup is pd.NA, with no language fallback. building_localization Nullable string / display text Localized production-method row's building. Only with language on a nonempty production-method table. building_group_localization Nullable string / display text Localized building's building_group. With language if its source column exists. production_method_group_localization Nullable string / display text Localized production-method row's group key. Only with language on a nonempty production-method table. production_method_localization Nullable string / display text Localized production-method row's method key. Only with language on a nonempty production-method table.

Localized text preserves raw game references, formatting, icons, and functions; the parser does not evaluate them. Localization columns are placed beside their identifier. Raw script identifiers remain the join keys.

docs.title: Buildings and building groups
docs.text:
BuildingsParser.to_dataframe() has one row per building. BuildingGroupParser.to_dataframe() has one row per group and does not resolve inheritance. The building export joins the group's resolved scalar attributes. Nested dict/Tree attributes are omitted; lists are +-joined.

Column or family Type / unit Meaning / transformation Presence / edge cases required_construction_points Integer / construction points per level Resolves a building's required_construction script-value name through common/script_values (construction_cost_*). Absent when no reference exists; unknown references warn and skip the value. Other rows can then have NaN in this column. land_usage String / category Joined group value: urban or rural, inherited from the first ancestor that specifies it when missing locally. Unresolved values remain absent/missing; raw group export does not apply inheritance. cash_reserves_max Number / £ per level Joined group cash-reserve ceiling, inherited when missing or zero. An ancestor's zero is also skipped; no reachable value leaves the original value unchanged. economy_of_scale Boolean / flag Joined group eligibility, inherited when missing from the child group. Explicit false is retained; the production table additionally excludes subsistence buildings. building_group_<attribute> Source-dependent / inherited source unit Collision-prefixed joined group attribute when its name already exists in the building row. For example, building_group_land_usage. Collision handling is per row; the concrete attributes are game-defined. Building values are preserved.

Other joined scalar group attributes remain group-local rather than inherited. Parent-chain traversal stops at unknown parents or cycles. A missing group reference warns and skips the join. These are transformations, not a claim that every named field exists in every input definition.

docs.title: Production methods
docs.text:
ProductionMethodParser.to_dataframe() has one row per building/production-method-group/production-method membership, not one row per complete building configuration. The same method can occur in multiple rows. Scalar method attributes are passed through, lists are +-joined, and nested containers are omitted. The computed families below are zero-filled.

Column or family Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases building String / identifier Building whose production-method group contains this method. Fixed row identifier. production_method_group String / identifier Group providing the method choice. Fixed row identifier; unknown referenced groups raise an error. production_method String / identifier Single chosen method in that group. Fixed row identifier; complete combinations are formed by production_table(). employment Number / workers per level Sum of building_employment_* values in the method's level_scaled building modifiers. Zero when absent; negative automation adjustments are retained. employment_<profession> Number / workers per level Value of building_employment_<profession>_add; e.g. employment_laborers. Family discovered from employment modifiers; absent method/profession values are zero. goods_<good> Number / goods units per week per level Signed workforce_scaled goods modifier: output positive, input negative; e.g. goods_tools. Accepts goods_(output\|input)_<good>_add and legacy building_(output\|input)_<good>_add names. One column per supplied/parsed good; absent flows zero. The parser assigns matched modifiers rather than resolving arbitrary game effects.

State-modifier keys are also flattened from unscaled, level_scaled, and workforce_scaled blocks and zero-filled across rows. Their concrete names and units are game-defined and excluded from the enumerated dictionary. Flattening drops the scaling-block distinction; duplicate keys across blocks of a method raise ValueError. One explicitly consumed modifier, state_infrastructure_add, represents infrastructure generation in the production table's net-footprint calculation; it is present in the method table only if discovered in the inputs.

docs.title: Technologies
docs.text:
One row per technology. Nested dict/Tree blocks are omitted and lists are +-joined; remaining scalar attributes are passed through.

Column Type / unit Meaning / transformation Presence / edge cases era Integer / era number Converts source era_N to numeric N. Converted when present; an unparsable era raises ValueError. The parser does not synthesize a missing era.

docs.title: Population needs
docs.text:
PopNeedsParser.to_dataframe() emits one row per need/good substitution entry. Rows are identified by the need key and eligible good. These six columns remain present in an empty result; localization is optional.

Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases key String / identifier Population need to which the entry belongs. Repeats across eligible goods. goods String / identifier Good allowed to satisfy the need, from the entry's goods. Missing entry field remains missing. weight Number / relative weight Base substitution weight applied to the good based on market sell-order share, preserved without normalization. Defaults to 1 when absent. max_supply_share Number / fraction Sell-order share ceiling above which additional relative supply no longer increases the applied base weight. Defaults to 1; stored rather than enforced by the parser. min_supply_share Number / fraction Minimum multiplier of base weight applied regardless of the good's sell-order share. Defaults to 0; stored rather than enforced by the parser. is_default Boolean / flag Whether the entry's good equals the need's default good. Computed by equality; a need without entries raises an error.

docs.title: Buy packages
docs.text:
buy_packages() emits one row per matching wealth_N definition, sorted by numeric wealth. popneed_* entries represent population needs, not individual tradeable goods. Game buy packages express base-value budgets for 10,000 working adults. The values below retain those source amounts, not converted physical goods quantities or realized demand from Economy.

Column or family Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases wealth Integer / wealth level Numeric N extracted from the wealth_N key. Nonmatching definitions are skipped. political_strength Number / source political-strength factor The wealth definition's political_strength. Missing source value remains missing; not included in the needs total. total_popneeds Number / £ base-value budget per 10,000 working adults Sum of all popneed_* values in this wealth row. Zero when no matching needs exist; no population scaling is performed. popneed_<need> Number / £ base-value budget per 10,000 working adults Need amount from the definition's goods block; e.g. popneed_basic_food. Columns follow first-seen order; absence at a wealth level is zero-filled.

docs.title: State regions
docs.text:
One row per state region. Arbitrary scalar attributes are passed through; nested attributes and province/trait/arable-resource lists are omitted, apart from the transformations below.

Column or family Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases province_count Integer / provinces Counts all provinces entries in the parsed region tree. Zero when none are found; does not subtract impassable provinces. resource_<building> Integer / potential building levels Capacity from capped_resources, or undiscovered_amount + discovered_amount from a resource block. Example: resource_building_oil_rig. Only encountered resource types become columns; missing/non-numeric cells are coerced to zero and converted to integers. undiscovered_amount_resource_<building> Integer / building levels Undiscovered component of a resource block. Defaults to zero within the block; exists only for encountered resource-block types. discovered_amount_resource_<building> Integer / building levels Discovered component of a resource block. Defaults to zero within the block; not synthesized for capped-resource entries.

These capacities describe definitions, not a save game's current discoveries or exploitation. state_region_resource_limits() uses total-potential resource_* columns only. It sums selected regions once each, treats missing/non-numeric values as zero, adds gold-field potential to gold-mine capacity, and sets gold-field capacity to zero. The separate arable-land helper sums the source arable_land field; that raw attribute is not synthesized by the parser.

docs.title: Goods and population types
docs.text:
Beyond the shared key and optional key_localization, these tables preserve game-defined attributes and do not add analytical columns. Population types omit nested containers and +-join lists. Goods preserve the source attribute values directly, including any nested values. The model consumes goods cost as base price and population-type start_quality_of_life, wage_weight, and paid_private_wage; their role in derived metrics is documented on the production and economy pages.

See the parsing API for constructors and source directories.

docs.title: Production configurations
docs.text: production_table() and production_table.csv contain one row per enumerated building configuration: one method from each of the building's method groups. The building and complete production_method string identify the row. The table does not filter combinations by a particular scenario or all gameplay conditions. Values describe one fully staffed building level, before throughput bonuses, and use goods base prices. See shared conventions.

docs.title: Identity, metadata, and requirements
docs.text: Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases building String / identifier Source building key. Always included. building_localization Nullable string / display text Building label propagated from the buildings input. Only if its input localization column exists; unknown labels are pd.NA. production_method String / identifiers Selected method keys joined by +, in building method-group order. Always included; identifies a complete combination. production_method_localization Nullable string / display text Selected method labels joined by +. Only if method localization input exists; any missing label makes the whole result pd.NA. building_group String / identifier Building's immediate group. Always included from buildings input. building_group_localization Nullable string / display text Propagated label for that group. Only with the buildings input's group localization column. parent_group Nullable string / identifier Parent group metadata joined onto the source building. Defaults to pd.NA when the source column is absent; not the entire ancestor chain. land_usage Nullable string / category Source building's resolved land-use category. Defaults to pd.NA if absent; see parser inheritance rules. is_subsistence Boolean / flag Source subsistence-building flag. Missing values/column become false. discoverable_resource Boolean / flag Source discoverable-resource flag. Missing values/column become false; not a numerical resource cap. depletable_resource Boolean / flag Source depletable-resource flag. Missing values/column become false; no depletion is simulated. economy_of_scale Boolean / eligibility flag Source economy_of_scale is true and source is_subsistence is false. Missing flags become false; eligibility does not apply a throughput bonus to this table. urbanization Number / urbanization points per level Source building's urbanization contribution. Missing value becomes zero. infrastructure_usage_per_level Number / infrastructure points per level Source infrastructure usage minus the sum of chosen methods' state_infrastructure_add. Missing usage becomes zero; absent modifier column warns and is zero-filled. Negative means provision. era Integer / era number Maximum era of the building's and chosen methods' unlocking technologies. Only with df_tech; zero if no required technologies; unknown required technologies raise an error. unlocking_tech String / identifiers Building requirements followed by chosen method requirements, deduplicated in first-seen order and joined by +. Always included; empty string for no requirements. unlocking_tech_localization Nullable string / display text Required technology labels joined by +. Only with a localized technology input; empty requirements or any missing label yield pd.NA. construction_cost Integer / construction points per level Building's resolved required_construction_points. Missing cost becomes zero; construction cost is not subtracted from weekly profit.

docs.title: Employment and goods flows
docs.text:
Column or family Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases employment Number / workers per level Sum of chosen methods' total employment. Always included; includes automation adjustments. employment_<profession> Number / workers per level Sum of chosen methods' profession-specific employment; e.g. employment_engineers. One column per profession present in the methods input. wage_normalized_employment Number / private-wage-equivalent workers per level Sum of profession employment times wage_weight, counting only professions whose paid_private_wage flag is true. Only with df_pop_types; missing private-wage flags default to true, including when the column is absent in older game data. Invalid or missing required profession weights raise an error. goods_<good> Number / goods units per week per level Sum of the chosen methods' signed flow for the good: positive output, negative input. One per goods-table key, in goods-table row order; missing methods input columns warn and are zero-filled. Unpriced goods columns are ignored with a warning. input_ratio_goods_<good> Float / fraction max(-goods_<good>, 0) / sum(max(-goods_<all goods>, 0)). Immediately follows its goods column. Zero for outputs, zero flows, and configurations without net inputs.

The input ratios use physical net-input quantities, not base-value shares. They sum to one when net inputs exist, otherwise zero. They cannot recover inputs offset by outputs of the same good. Prestige variants share the base good's column. Victoria 3's prestige-goods throughput bonus uses gross input base value; multiplying these ratios by the game's 20% maximum gives only a quantity-based analytical proxy.

For example, net inputs of 10 tools and 30 coal have quantity shares 0.25 and 0.75 regardless of their different prices. A net output contributes zero.

docs.title: Nominal economic metrics
docs.text:
Let q_g be the row's signed goods flow, p_g the goods base price, I = sum(max(-q_g, 0) * p_g), and O = sum(max(q_g, 0) * p_g). Let L be employment, W wage-normalized employment, and C construction cost. These input/output valuations split net flows; payroll is not subtracted. All monetary flows are weekly.

Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases value_goods_inputs_nominal Float / £ per week per level I: base-price value of negative net goods flows. Zero when no net inputs. value_goods_outputs_nominal Float / £ per week per level O: base-price value of positive net goods flows. Zero when no net outputs. profit_nominal Float / £ per week per level O - I, modeled goods-value surplus. Can be negative; excludes wages and construction expenditure. profit_margin_nominal Float / fraction (O - I) / O. Ordinary division; negative infinity if output value is zero and profit is negative, NaN for zero/zero. profit_per_capita_nominal Float / £ per worker per week (O - I) / L. Per employed worker; zero denominator can yield signed infinity or NaN. profit_per_wage_normalized_employment_nominal Float / £ per wage-equivalent worker per week (O - I) / W. Only with df_pop_types; ordinary division, with no payroll subtraction. profit_per_construction_cost_nominal Float / £ per week per construction point (O - I) / C. Ordinary division; zero construction cost can yield signed infinity or NaN.

Weekly profit and the per-worker/per-construction profit rates can be multiplied by 52 for annual equivalents. Do not annualize profit_margin_nominal or input shares. Missing localized text and undefined numeric ratios can both appear as blank CSV cells, but have different meanings.

See the economy and production API and parsing guide.

docs.title: Supply-chain reports
docs.text: SupplyChainAnalyzer solves a nominal scenario for exactly one positive target good. Its immutable result exposes the reports below. All schemas remain present when a report is empty. See shared conventions and the supply-chain guide.

docs.title: Scope, prices, and graph views
docs.text:
• System means every configuration in the solved state, including any production outside the terminal good's upstream chain.
  • Chain means processes in the realized terminal graph: active upstream producers, with their input goods and all coproduct outputs retained. Each included process contributes its whole employment, cost, and value added; nothing is allocated to individual coproducts.
  • realized graphs start from configurations whose level exceeds tolerance (default 1e-9). allowed graphs start from configurations not disabled by the era cap, PM bans, exact building-group bans, or building limits at or below tolerance. Both are restricted to the terminal's upstream graph and attached coproducts. Allowed membership does not prove LP feasibility.
  • processes(view), goods(view), and flows(view) use the requested graph, defaulting to realized. Even in allowed, quantities use the same solved levels; inactive alternatives do not get hypothetical production.
  • Input/output coefficients include the compiled fixed throughput multiplier. It scales goods, not employment, construction, land, or infrastructure. Coefficients split production-table net flows into positive input/output magnitudes; flows already offset in that table cannot be recovered.
  • Prices are state prices: base prices for the public nominal analyzer. The market automobile example at the end of this page has a separate schema.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
result.summary() is a Series with these fixed fields and the resource-building column families below, named after the terminal good. Sweeps turn them into columns. On a successful analyzer result, all fields are present. Let Q denote whole-system terminal net output, G_chain chain weekly value added, and L_chain chain employment. Safe division returns zero only for an exactly zero denominator.

Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases scenario String / label Scenario.display_name(). Uses explicit scenario name or the generated display name. terminal_good String / identifier The single good being analyzed. Has positive aggregated exports in the scenario. objective String / category Nominal objective: gdp, employment, automation, or construction_cost. gdp_per_capita is rejected by the analyzer. solver_status Integer / status code HiGHS result status. Successful solves normally report 0; sweep failures use synthetic -1. solver_message String / diagnostic text HiGHS message retained from the solve. Sweep failures instead retain the exception message. objective_value Float / objective units Whole-system attained objective: weekly GDP (£/week), employment (workers), automation (workers), or construction points. Sign restored for maximized GDP/employment; not necessarily a chain-only metric. target_quantity Float / goods units per week Aggregated terminal export orders. Strictly positive; imports may cover some or all demand. target_base_value Float / £ per week Target quantity times terminal state price. Equals base value in nominal analysis; sweep preserves effective terminal export value on failure. terminal_base_price Float / £ per goods unit Terminal price from the state. Base price in nominal analysis; not an annual rate. terminal_gross_output Float / goods units per week Whole-system terminal building_goods_output. Before subtracting terminal consumption by processes. terminal_net_output Float / goods units per week Q = levels @ net_matrix[:, terminal]. Whole-system output minus process inputs; not reduced by exports or population orders. terminal_surplus Float / goods units per week terminal_net_output + terminal imports - terminal exports - min_goods_balance. Slack above the household-excluding balance floor; can be slightly negative within solver tolerance. system_gdp_weekly Float / £ per week Sum of system output minus input quantities valued at state prices.
