Excludes payroll; imports/exports are not separately added to GDP. system_gdp_annual Float / £ per year 52 * system_gdp_weekly. Annualization only, not a second solve. chain_gdp_weekly Float / £ per week G_chain = sum(realized process value_added). Includes entire coproduct values of included processes. chain_gdp_annual Float / £ per year 52 * chain_gdp_weekly. Same process scope as weekly chain GDP. system_employment Float / workers Sum of all state employment. Model population means employed workers. chain_employment Float / workers L_chain = sum(realized process employment). No allocation to individual output goods. system_construction_cost Float / construction points Whole-system levels dotted with construction coefficients. A stock of required construction, not a weekly cost. chain_construction_cost Float / construction points Sum of realized process construction costs. Can be zero for zero-cost configurations. system_arable_land Float / arable-land units Whole-system levels dotted with land coefficients. Uses the immediate agricultural group rule on the economy dictionary page. chain_arable_land Float / arable-land units Sum of realized process arable land. Zero when no included process consumes modeled arable land. system_net_infrastructure_usage Float / infrastructure points Whole-system levels dotted with net infrastructure coefficients. Negative means net infrastructure provision. chain_net_infrastructure_usage Float / infrastructure points Sum of realized process net infrastructure usage. Also signed; not an absolute consumption total. employment_per_terminal_unit Float / workers per unit/week of output capacity L_chain / Q. Safe division; denominator is net system output, not the target or gross output. construction_per_terminal_unit Float / construction points per unit/week of output capacity chain_construction_cost / Q. Safe division; construction is not annualized. gdp_per_terminal_unit Float / £ per terminal goods unit G_chain / Q. Both GDP and net production are weekly; their time factors cancel. output_per_10k_workers Float / goods units per week per 10,000 workers Q * 10000 / L_chain. Safe division; zero if chain employment is exactly zero. realized_process_count Integer / nodes Number of configurations in the realized graph. Counts configurations, not summed building levels. realized_good_count Integer / nodes Number of good nodes in the realized graph. Includes terminal and attached coproduct goods. realized_edge_count Integer / edges Number of directed goods/process edges in the realized graph. Input and output edges count separately. allowed_process_count Integer / nodes Number of configurations in the allowed graph. Includes inactive alternatives upstream of the terminal. allowed_good_count Integer / nodes Number of good nodes in the allowed graph. Does not count every good in the economy. allowed_edge_count Integer / edges Number of directed edges in the allowed graph. Not the number of diagram edges after visualization pruning. cyclic_component_count Integer / components Realized strongly connected components with more than one node, or a self-loop. Zero for an acyclic graph. cyclic_node_count Integer / nodes Number of realized nodes participating in a directed cycle. Counts both goods and process nodes. condensation_depth Integer / edges Longest directed-path length after each realized strongly connected component becomes one node. Zero for an empty or single-component condensation; counts bipartite graph edges. extractive_process_count Integer / configurations Count of realized processes marked is_extractive. Uses immediate parent bg_extraction or either resource flag. resource_process_count Integer / configurations Count with discoverable_resource or depletable_resource. A process with both flags counts once; not resource capacity or remaining stock. chain_gdp_share Float / signed ratio chain_gdp_weekly / system_gdp_weekly. Safe division; negative or offsetting contributions can put the ratio outside [0, 1]. chain_employment_share Float / fraction chain_employment / system_employment. Safe division. chain_construction_share Float / fraction chain_construction_cost / system_construction_cost. Safe division. chain_arable_land_share Float / fraction chain_arable_land / system_arable_land. Safe division. chain_infrastructure_share Float / signed ratio chain_net_infrastructure_usage / system_net_infrastructure_usage. Safe division; cancellation and negative values mean it need not lie in [0, 1]. system_gdp_per_capita_weekly Float / £ per person per week system_gdp_weekly * workforce_ratio / system_employment. Safe division; includes uniformly inferred dependents. system_gdp_per_capita_annual Float / £ per person per year 52 * system_gdp_per_capita_weekly. Included in every summary and sweep, including the video export. chain_gdp_per_capita_weekly Float / £ per person per week chain_gdp_weekly * workforce_ratio / chain_employment. Safe division; includes whole-process coproduct contributions. chain_gdp_per_capita_annual Float / £ per person per year 52 * chain_gdp_per_capita_weekly. Same realized-chain scope. system_wage_normalized_employment Float / private-wage-equivalent workers Sum of system levels times production-table wage_normalized_employment. NaN if the column or any contributing coefficient is unavailable/nonfinite; inactive missing coefficients are ignored. chain_wage_normalized_employment Float / private-wage-equivalent workers Sum of realized-chain levels times production-table wage_normalized_employment. Same missing-data policy, restricted to contributing chain processes. system_gdp_per_wage_normalized_employment_weekly Float / £ per wage-equivalent worker per week system_gdp_weekly / system_wage_normalized_employment. Safe division; NaN when wage coefficients are unavailable. system_gdp_per_wage_normalized_employment_annual Float / £ per wage-equivalent worker per year 52 * system_gdp_per_wage_normalized_employment_weekly. NaN when wage coefficients are unavailable. chain_gdp_per_wage_normalized_employment_weekly Float / £ per wage-equivalent worker per week chain_gdp_weekly / chain_wage_normalized_employment. Safe division; NaN when contributing chain wage coefficients are unavailable. chain_gdp_per_wage_normalized_employment_annual Float / £ per wage-equivalent worker per year 52 * chain_gdp_per_wage_normalized_employment_weekly. Same realized-chain scope. system_gdp_per_construction_cost_weekly Float / £ per construction point per week system_gdp_weekly / system_construction_cost. Safe division; construction is a stock, not a weekly expense. system_gdp_per_construction_cost_annual Float / £ per construction point per year 52 * system_gdp_per_construction_cost_weekly. Annualizes GDP only. chain_gdp_per_construction_cost_weekly Float / £ per construction point per week chain_gdp_weekly / chain_construction_cost. Safe division; includes all construction of realized-chain processes. chain_gdp_per_construction_cost_annual Float / £ per construction point per year 52 * chain_gdp_per_construction_cost_weekly. Annualizes GDP only.

Graph counts use the complete retained graphs. They are independent of the top-producer pruning used by a plotted or Mermaid allowed view.

docs.title: Resource building levels
docs.text:
These summary column families use full building identifiers, for example chain_levels_building_coal_mine and chain_levels_per_10k_pop_building_coal_mine. Extraction membership uses the same rule as is_extractive: immediate parent bg_extraction, or a discoverable or depletable resource flag. This includes ordinary mines, logging camps, fishing wharves, whaling stations, rubber plantations, and oil rigs. Farms, ranches, and other arable-land plantations remain represented by arable land.

Types come from the full economy production table, including banned and unused types. Columns follow the fixed summary fields, sorted by building identifier; within each type, system raw/normalized levels precede chain raw/normalized levels. All summaries from one economy share this schema, even empty sweeps and all-failure sweeps. Successful unused types are zero; failed solves are NaN.

Column family Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases system_levels_<building> Float / building levels Sum of all solved configuration levels for this extraction building type. Fractional levels are retained; no aggregate resource-level total is added. system_levels_per_10k_pop_<building> Float / levels per 10,000 workers system_levels_<building> * 10000 / system_employment. Safe division; excludes dependents and unemployed people. chain_levels_<building> Float / building levels Sum of realized-chain configuration levels for this extraction building type. Multiple PM configurations of one building type are combined. chain_levels_per_10k_pop_<building> Float / levels per 10,000 workers chain_levels_<building> * 10000 / chain_employment. Safe division; 5 levels and 2,000 chain workers give 25 levels per 10,000 workers.

docs.title: Processes
docs.text:
result.processes(view) has one row per configuration in the requested graph, in production-table row order. Let x be its solved level, m its throughput multiplier, I its adjusted input value per level, and O its adjusted output value per level. Unit economics retain all output goods.

Here, process means a building with its complete PM combination, rather than the building type alone. The guide explains the naming rationale and parallels with Brightway.

Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases building String / identifier Source building key. Multiple configurations may share it. production_method String / compound identifiers Complete chosen method combination. Methods are joined by +. building_group String / identifier Immediate source building group. Missing metadata defaults to empty string. parent_group String / identifier Immediate parent metadata of that group. Missing metadata defaults to empty string. land_usage String / category Source resolved land-use metadata. Missing metadata defaults to empty string; not the land coefficient itself. era Integer / era number Source configuration era. Required by the reporting implementation. allowed Boolean / membership flag Process node is in the terminal's allowed graph. Graph membership, not independent LP feasibility. active Boolean / solved flag x > tolerance. May be false in the allowed view. in_terminal_chain Boolean / membership flag Configuration appears in the realized terminal graph. An active process elsewhere in the system can still be false. level Float / building levels x, from the whole solved state. Fractional or zero levels are valid. throughput_multiplier Float / multiplier Compiled fixed goods multiplier m. 1 means unchanged; excludes level-dependent economy of scale. unit_input_cost Float / £ per week per level I = adjusted input row @ state prices. Includes throughput; zero with no modeled inputs. unit_output_value Float / £ per week per level O = adjusted output row @ state prices. Includes every coproduct. unit_value_added Float / £ per week per level O - I. Can be negative; excludes wages. input_cost Float / £ per week I * x. Zero for a zero-level allowed alternative. output_value Float / £ per week O * x. Zero for a zero-level allowed alternative. value_added Float / £ per week (O - I) * x. Entire process contribution, not allocated to one good. employment Float / workers Per-level employment coefficient times x. Not multiplied by m. construction_cost Float / construction points Per-level construction coefficient times x. Not multiplied by m. arable_land Float / arable-land units Per-level land coefficient times x. Uses immediate group membership; not multiplied by m. net_infrastructure_usage Float / infrastructure points Per-level net infrastructure coefficient times x. Signed; not multiplied by m. is_extractive Boolean / classification flag Immediate parent_group == "bg_extraction" or either resource flag in allowed-graph metadata. Defaults false if no matching metadata; does not traverse ancestors. is_subsistence Boolean / source flag Source subsistence metadata. Missing metadata defaults false. discoverable_resource Boolean / source flag Source discoverable-resource metadata. Missing metadata defaults false. depletable_resource Boolean / source flag Source depletable-resource metadata. Missing metadata defaults false; depletion is not simulated.

docs.title: Goods
docs.text:
result.goods(view) has one row per good node in the requested graph, in economy goods order. Production and consumption sum only processes in that view, while imports, exports, and population orders come from the whole state. This mix of scopes means these balances need not equal whole-system market balances. Producer counts use the two retained graphs irrespective of the requested view.

Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases good String / identifier Good key. Includes attached coproduct goods. terminal Boolean / flag Whether this is the analyzed terminal good. True only for the terminal key. price Float / £ per goods unit State price for this good. Base price in nominal analysis. production Float / goods units per week View-process levels times adjusted output coefficients. Zero is valid for an input-only good or inactive allowed production. consumption Float / goods units per week View-process levels times adjusted input coefficients. Positive magnitude, not a negative signed flow. imports Float / goods units per week Whole-state imported orders. Zero when no imports supplied. exports Float / goods units per week Whole-state exported orders. Zero when no exports supplied. pop_needs Float / goods units per week Whole-state calculated household demand. Zero for nominal supply-chain solves. sell_orders Float / goods units per week View production + imports. Combines view and state scope. buy_orders Float / goods units per week View consumption + exports + pop_needs. Combines view and state scope. net_balance Float / goods units per week sell_orders - buy_orders. Signed; differs from terminal net production. output_value Float / £ per week View production * price. Imports are not included. input_value Float / £ per week View consumption * price. Exports/population orders are not included. input_cost_share Float / fraction input_value / total input value of all view processes. Safe division; zero when total input value is zero. allowed_producers Integer / configurations Process predecessors of this good in the allowed graph. Restricted graph count, not every producer in the economy. active_producers Integer / configurations Process predecessors of this good in the realized graph. Count unaffected by view; does not sum their levels.

docs.title: Flows
docs.text:
result.flows(view) has one row per directed graph edge, sorted by the source and target node strings. Inputs point from goods to processes; outputs point from processes to goods. Rates and amounts are positive magnitudes.

Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases source String / node identifier Edge source: good:<key> or process:<config>. Direction depends on role. target String / node identifier Edge target: process:<config> or good:<key>. Direction depends on role. role String / category input or output. Distinguishes flow direction without a signed rate. good String / identifier Good carried by this edge. Same key as the goods report. process String / configuration identifier Configuration key, without the process: prefix. Same key as process config. unit_rate Float / goods units per week per level Adjusted input or output coefficient. Includes throughput; edges are created only for coefficients > 0. realized_amount Float / goods units per week unit_rate * solved process level. Can be zero for an allowed alternative. price Float / £ per goods unit State price for the edge's good. Base price in nominal analysis. realized_value Float / £ per week realized_amount * price. Zero for an inactive flow. active Boolean / flow flag realized_amount > tolerance. Amount threshold, distinct from process level threshold. in_cycle Boolean / endpoint flag Both endpoints are cyclic nodes in the requested graph. Does not require them to belong to the same cyclic component; do not interpret it as an exact cycle-edge test.

docs.title: Workforce
docs.text:
result.workforce() uses only realized-chain configurations, in row order then profession order. It omits process/profession employment at or below tolerance.

Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases config String / configuration identifier Configuration employing the profession. Matches process building + "+" + production_method. building String / identifier Configuration's source building. Multiple rows can share it. profession String / identifier Profession key from the economy's profession index. No row for employment at or below tolerance. employment Float / workers State employment cell for this configuration/profession. Per-level profession coefficient times solved level; throughput does not change it.

docs.title: Constraints and bottlenecks
docs.text:
result.constraints() exposes compiled LP rows, inequalities first and equalities second, in their named slice order. Constraints apply to the whole system. Inequalities are stored in canonical form A_ub @ levels <= b_ub; for example the goods-balance floor uses negative net-production coefficients and a bound of imports - exports - min_goods_balance. Interpret the compiled sign before converting a marginal to a gameplay change. Variable bounds are not rows in this report.

Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases kind String / category inequality or equality. Determines slack/residual interpretation. family String / constraint identifier Named compiled constraint slice, such as min_goods_balance or building_level_caps. Only families present in the compiled problem appear. label String / row label Good/building/group key for applicable families; PM bans use their +-joined keys; other rows use the family name. If label count differs from row count, uses family[i]. realized_value Float / compiled row units A_row @ solved levels. Signed canonical left-hand side, not always the physical quantity named by the family. bound Float / compiled row units Stored right-hand side b_row. A lower-bound target can be represented as a negative bound. slack Float / compiled row units For inequalities, bound - realized_value. NaN for equalities; slightly negative values can occur within solver tolerance. residual Float / compiled row units For equalities, realized_value - bound. Exactly 0 in this column for inequalities. binding Boolean / threshold flag Inequality slack <= tolerance; equality abs(residual) <= tolerance. Numerical criterion, not proof that relaxing the row improves the objective. solver_marginal Float / solver objective units per compiled bound unit Raw HiGHS derivative of its minimized objective with respect to this right-hand side. NaN if diagnostics unavailable; GDP/employment objectives are negated for minimization. improvement_per_unit Float / solver objective units per compiled bound unit For a finite inequality marginal, max(0, -solver_marginal). NaN for equalities or unavailable/nonfinite marginals; local sensitivity to increasing the canonical bound.

For minimized construction/automation, positive improvement means lowering the minimized cost. For maximized GDP/employment, it means increasing the reported objective. It measures one unit of the compiled RHS, so relaxing a negative production constraint means lowering its requested physical minimum. It is local LP sensitivity and is not a guaranteed finite-change benefit.

result.bottlenecks() returns the same columns, restricted to binding inequalities with improvement_per_unit > tolerance, sorted by improvement descending, then family and label. It has no separate schema.

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text:
result.alternatives(good) lists producer predecessors of the specified good in the terminal's allowed graph. With no argument it covers all goods in that graph. It sorts by good, selected first, unit output descending, then config. Unit costs and values describe the entire process, not only the requested good. “Selected” means membership in the realized chain, not simply a positive level anywhere in the system.

Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases good String / identifier Good for which this process is an alternative producer. A coproduct process can appear once per output good. config String / configuration identifier Allowed producer configuration key. No row if the good has no producer in the allowed graph. building String / identifier Source building key. Same metadata as the process report. production_method String / compound identifiers Complete method combination. +-joined. era Integer / era number Configuration's required era. Same metadata as the process report. unit_output Float / goods units per week per level Adjusted output coefficient for this good. Includes throughput, unlike the all-goods monetary unit fields. unit_input_cost Float / £ per week per level Whole adjusted process input row valued at state prices. Includes all process inputs. unit_output_value Float / £ per week per level Whole adjusted process output row valued at state prices. Includes every coproduct. unit_value_added Float / £ per week per level unit_output_value - unit_input_cost. Excludes wages; can be negative. selected Boolean / membership flag Configuration occurs in the realized terminal graph. False for alternatives outside that chain, even if active elsewhere. level Float / building levels Whole-state solved level of the configuration. Zero allowed for an inactive alternative. parent_group String / identifier Parent metadata from the allowed graph. Missing metadata defaults to empty string. land_usage String / category Land-use metadata from the allowed graph. Missing metadata defaults to empty string. is_extractive Boolean / classification flag Immediate parent bg_extraction or either resource flag. No ancestor traversal. is_subsistence Boolean / source flag Source subsistence flag. Missing metadata defaults false. discoverable_resource Boolean / source flag Source discoverable-resource flag. Missing metadata defaults false. depletable_resource Boolean / source flag Source depletable-resource flag. Missing metadata defaults false.

docs.title: Sweep summary and failures
docs.text:
sweep_supply_chains() generates one scenario per requested good, preserving the requested order (by default economy.producible_goods order). Each quantity is target_value / base_price; every requested base price must be finite and positive. sweep.summary contains these fields followed by all summary fields. sweep.failures is the failed subset with the same columns and a reset index, including when empty.

Column Type / unit Meaning / calculation Presence / edge cases good String / identifier Good selected for this sweep row. Matches terminal_good; retained on failures. status String / category success or failure. Failed solves do not stop subsequent goods. error_type String / exception name Type of caught analysis exception. Empty on success; currently ValueError on recorded failures. error_message String / diagnostic text Caught exception message. Empty on success; retained on failure.

On failure, scenario, terminal good, objective, effective terminal export quantity and base value, and terminal base price remain populated. solver_status becomes -1 and solver_message becomes the exception text. All remaining summary fields are NaN, including counts and objective_value; they do not mean zero. Sweep input-validation errors raise before an applicable result rather than becoming failure rows. For each terminal good, exports are the higher of aggregated template exports and target_value / base_price; other exports and all imports are retained.

sweep.df_building_levels is a float matrix with one row per production unit in economy.building_index order and one column per requested terminal good in selection order. Its index is named config and uses the existing building+production_method keys, keeping PM combinations separate. Each successful column contains the complete solved state.building_levels vector, including production outside the realized terminal chain, fractional levels, and zero levels for unused units. Failed columns contain NaN throughout. An empty sweep retains every production-unit row with zero columns. This report is available with keep_results=False and returns a defensive copy.

docs.title: Example CSV additions
docs.text:
The nominal example exports retain every sweep field, including its failure policy, and add these labels. The comparison summary.csv has one row per configuration/good pair; video summary.csv files have one row per variant/good pair. Detailed results live under analyses/supply_chains/<configuration>/<good>/; cross-good summary.csv files live at configuration level. Cross-configuration comparisons live under analyses/supply_chains/comparison/summary.csv, alongside the population, construction, and annual GDP per capita charts pop.svg, construction_points.svg, and gdp_per_capita.svg. Labels describe presets, not additional economic metrics.

The comparison example also writes analyses/supply_chains/<configuration>/building_levels.csv beside each configuration's summary. Its first column is config, followed by one column per requested good; failed solves are blank cells. Empty selections produce only the config column with every production unit retained.

Column Type / unit Meaning / source Presence / edge cases configuration String / preset label Scenario preset in examples/supply_chain_compare.py. In comparison and preset summary CSVs; rows retain it on failure. variant String / preset label base or a named product-specific variant in examples/supply_chain_cangshulun.py. Only in video summary CSVs; base covers all producible goods, named variants selected goods. ban_config String / preset label Ban-policy label supplied by the example. Retained on failure; an empty label in the comparison export does not mean no default building-group bans.

See the supply-chain API for report calls and the showcase for example downloads and commands.

docs.title: Design notes
docs.text:
These notes explain the model's calculation dependencies and architecture. For workflows, start with the guides; for exact output definitions, see the data dictionary.

  • Economy dependencies: signal-flow graphs showing production preparation, consumption, market prices, household finances, wealth iteration, and the owner of each value.
  • Supply-chain design references: architectural parallels with graph, optimization, accounting, and coproduct-allocation tools.

docs.title: Economy dependencies
docs.text:
These graphs describe the current economy model. An arrow means the source is needed to calculate the target; it does not imply that every solve mode runs that calculation. Dashed arrows carry wealth into the next iteration. Repeated node names refer to the same value across graphs. Wide diagrams scroll horizontally to preserve readable labels.

For usage, see the economy guide. The API reference describes the public interfaces, and the economy data dictionary defines report units and accounting boundaries.

docs.title: Storage legend
docs.text:
• E Economy: game tables and model coefficients.
  • C EconomyContext: fixed inputs shared by snapshots.
  • M MarketState: prices and building finances.
  • P PopState: household wealth, demand, and finances.
  • S EconomyState: the composed snapshot and combined reports.
  • V A separate argument, returned value, constant, or solver working variable.

An asterisk (*) marks a cached property. Methods ending in () calculate their return values on demand without caching them. Textual owner prefixes remain meaningful without color.

EconomyState holds context, market, and households references. Its flat properties, such as state.building_goods_flow and state.pop_income, forward to the component owners shown here; they do not duplicate the arrays.

docs.title: Production preparation
docs.text:
Building levels, production coefficients, and effective throughput determine realized weekly goods flows. Employment scales with building levels, while throughput changes goods inputs and outputs without scaling worker counts. Effective throughput adds the economy-of-scale bonus to the supplied multiplier.

---
config:
  flowchart:
    useMaxWidth: false
    nodeSpacing: 20
    rankSpacing: 35
  themeCSS: |
    .node.model rect { fill: var(--vic3-owner-economy) !important; }
    .node.context rect { fill: var(--vic3-owner-context) !important; }
    .node.variable rect { fill: var(--vic3-owner-variable) !important; }
    .node rect { stroke: var(--vic3-owner-border) !important; }
    .nodeLabel { color: var(--vic3-owner-text) !important; }
    .flowchart-link { stroke: var(--vic3-owner-edge) !important; }
    marker path { fill: var(--vic3-owner-edge) !important; stroke: var(--vic3-owner-edge) !important; }
    .edgeLabel, .edgeLabel p { color: var(--vic3-owner-text) !important; background: var(--md-default-bg-color) !important; }
---
flowchart TD
    DP["[E] df_production"]:::model
    PC["[E] Unscaled goods matrices *"]:::model
    EM["[E] employment_matrix *"]:::model
    DP --> PC
    DP --> EM

    L["[C] building_levels"]:::context
    CAP["[V] economy_of_scale_level_cap"]:::variable
    TM["[V] throughput_multipliers"]:::variable

    L --> EOS["[V] Economy-of-scale bonuses"]:::variable
    CAP --> EOS
    DP --> EOS
    EOS --> T["[V] Effective throughput"]:::variable
    TM --> T

    L --> F["[C] building_goods_flow"]:::context
    PC --> F
    T --> F

    F --> GI["[C] building_goods_input *"]:::context
    F --> GO["[C] building_goods_output *"]:::context

    GO --> SELL["[C] sell_orders *"]:::context

Flows retain the production table's signed-net convention within each configuration. Splitting signs before aggregation preserves opposing orders between different configurations. No separate gross-flow parsing is implied.

docs.title: Consumption and market prices
docs.text:
Economy.df_buy_packages contains raw need-category budgets at base prices. Prepared EconomyContext.goods_buy_packages is a GoodsBuyPackages object containing goods quantities by wealth tier and wealth row labels. These are different representations.

---
config:
  flowchart:
    useMaxWidth: false
    nodeSpacing: 20
    rankSpacing: 35
  themeCSS: |
    .node.model rect { fill: var(--vic3-owner-economy) !important; }
    .node.context rect { fill: var(--vic3-owner-context) !important; }
    .node.market rect { fill: var(--vic3-owner-market) !important; }
    .node.household rect { fill: var(--vic3-owner-pop) !important; }
    .node.snapshot rect { fill: var(--vic3-owner-state) !important; }
    .node.variable rect { fill: var(--vic3-owner-variable) !important; }
    .node rect { stroke: var(--vic3-owner-border) !important; }
    .nodeLabel { color: var(--vic3-owner-text) !important; }
    .flowchart-link { stroke: var(--vic3-owner-edge) !important; }
    marker path { fill: var(--vic3-owner-edge) !important; stroke: var(--vic3-owner-edge) !important; }
    .edgeLabel, .edgeLabel p { color: var(--vic3-owner-text) !important; background: var(--md-default-bg-color) !important; }
---
flowchart TD
    N["[C] pops"]:::context --> SC["[C] consumption_scales"]:::context
    R["[C] workforce_ratio"]:::context --> D["[C] dependents_per_worker *"]:::context
    D --> SC
    CM["[E] _pop_consumption_multipliers *"]:::model --> SC

    SELL["[C] sell_orders *"]:::context --> ES["[V] Effective substitution supply"]:::variable
    NP["[C] non_pop_buy_orders *"]:::context --> ES

    ES --> SH["[V] Substitution shares"]:::variable
    PN["[E] df_pop_needs"]:::model --> SH

    SH --> Q["[C] goods_buy_packages<br/>wealth + quantities"]:::context
    RAW["[E] df_buy_packages<br/>Raw category budgets"]:::model --> Q
    BASE["[E] base_prices *"]:::model --> Q
    Q --> QR["[V] df_goods_buy_packages()<br/>DataFrame export"]:::variable

    Q --> NEEDS["[P] pop_buy_orders"]:::household
    SC --> NEEDS
    W["[P] pop_wealth"]:::household --> NEEDS

    NEEDS --> BUY["[S] buy_orders *"]:::snapshot
    NP --> BUY

    BUY --> PRICE["[M] market_prices"]:::market
    SELL --> PRICE
    BASE --> PRICE

Prepared baskets and scales are optional context fields. prepare_context() computes only missing fields; supplied fields are authoritative. Baskets stay fixed while production, trade, and substitution assumptions are fixed. Scales stay fixed while worker counts, workforce ratio, and profession multipliers are fixed. Changing wealth selects different basket rows; changing prices changes their monetary cost rather than their quantities.

goods_buy_packages() returns immutable GoodsBuyPackages, reusing prepared baskets when present. Explicit, prepared, and freshly calculated baskets share one selection path in consumption calculations. df_goods_buy_packages() exports an independent DataFrame from a state, context, or basket object. pop_consumption_scales(), pop_buy_orders(), and pop_expenses() return arrays without updating a snapshot. Preparation and wealth evaluation attach the appropriate results to their owners. The evaluator calculates total buy orders as a working array; the composed snapshot exposes the same quantity through cached buy_orders.

docs.title: Household finances and iteration
docs.text:
Cooperative income distributes each configuration's positive value added according to worker counts and profession wage weights. Dependent earnings are added separately. Expenses value the selected baskets at the same market prices. Basket costs, income coefficients, and transitions are solver working values, rather than additional public state fields.

---
config:
  flowchart:
    useMaxWidth: false
    nodeSpacing: 20
    rankSpacing: 35
  themeCSS: |
    .node.model rect { fill: var(--vic3-owner-economy) !important; }
    .node.context rect { fill: var(--vic3-owner-context) !important; }
    .node.market rect { fill: var(--vic3-owner-market) !important; }
    .node.household rect { fill: var(--vic3-owner-pop) !important; }
    .node.variable rect { fill: var(--vic3-owner-variable) !important; }
    .node rect { stroke: var(--vic3-owner-border) !important; }
    .nodeLabel { color: var(--vic3-owner-text) !important; }
    .flowchart-link { stroke: var(--vic3-owner-edge) !important; }
    marker path { fill: var(--vic3-owner-edge) !important; stroke: var(--vic3-owner-edge) !important; }
    .edgeLabel, .edgeLabel p { color: var(--vic3-owner-text) !important; background: var(--md-default-bg-color) !important; }
---
flowchart TD
    F["[C] building_goods_flow"]:::context --> SUR["[M] building_surplus *"]:::market
    PRICE["[M] market_prices"]:::market --> SUR
    SUR --> DEF["[M] building_deficit *"]:::market

    N["[C] pops"]:::context --> SH["[V] Cooperative allocation shares"]:::variable
    WW["[E] pop_wage_weights *"]:::model --> SH

    SUR --> CI["[V] Cooperative income<br/>Positive surplus only"]:::variable
    SH --> CI

    N --> DI["[V] Dependent income"]:::variable
    D["[C] dependents_per_worker *"]:::context --> DI
    DW["[E] df_pop_types.dependent_wage"]:::model --> DI

    CI --> INC["[P] pop_income"]:::household
    DI --> INC

    Q["[C] goods_buy_packages<br/>wealth + quantities"]:::context --> BC["[V] Basket costs by wealth"]:::variable
    PRICE --> BC

    BC --> EXP["[P] pop_expenses"]:::household
    W["[P] pop_wealth at t"]:::household --> EXP
    SC["[C] consumption_scales"]:::context --> EXP

    INC --> BAL["[P] pop_balance *"]:::household
    EXP --> BAL

    BC --> COSTS["[V] Current- and next-tier<br/>household costs"]:::variable
    W --> COSTS
    SC --> COSTS

    COSTS --> RULE["[V] Wealth transition"]:::variable
    INC --> RULE
    W --> RULE
    TH["[V] 0.98 / 1.02 constants<br/>+ rtol / atol"]:::variable --> RULE

    RULE --> NW["[P] pop_wealth at t + 1"]:::household
    NW -. "Next evaluation" .-> W

evaluate_wealth(context, pop_wealth) evaluates one assignment without changing wealth and returns matching MarketState and PopState components. iterate() trusts consistent evaluated inputs, applies simultaneous one-tier changes using the previous prices and income, and evaluates the new assignment. It shares the fixed context and returns the original components when wealth is unchanged.

The transition decreases wealth below 98% of current-tier cost; otherwise it increases wealth at or above 102% of next-tier cost, within configured numerical tolerances. Decreases take precedence, and minimum/maximum tiers bound movement. solve(method="equilibrium") repeats evaluation and transition, detects cycles and iteration limits, and independently verifies a stationary result. Numerical convergence does not guarantee affordability at the minimum tier or funded building losses; equilibrium_diagnostics records these flags on EconomyState.

pop_income and pop_expenses are optional PopState fields. Nominal and market solves leave them unevaluated, and pop_balance is None until both are supplied. When evaluated, balance is the signed weekly difference between income and expenses; it is not an accumulated savings stock.

docs.title: Derived reports
docs.text:
Fixed population metrics belong to the context, price-valued production metrics belong to the market, and reports combining wealth with fixed population data belong to the composed economy snapshot.

    F["[C] building_goods_flow"]:::context --> GDP["[M] gdp_weekly *"]:::market

    GDP --> AGDP["[M] gdp(annual=True)"]:::market

    N["[C] pops"]:::context --> EMP["[C] total_employment *"]:::context
    EMP --> POP["[C] total_population *"]:::context
    R["[C] workforce_ratio"]:::context --> POP

    GDP --> GDPC["[S] gdp_per_capita()"]:::snapshot
    POP --> GDPC

    N --> EP["[C] employment_by_profession *"]:::context
    EP --> PS["[C] profession_shares *"]:::context
    EMP --> PS

    W["[P] pop_wealth"]:::household --> WT["[S] total_wealth_by_profession *"]:::snapshot
    N --> WT
    WT --> AW["[S] average_wealth *"]:::snapshot
    EMP --> AW
    WT --> WP["[S] average_wealth_by_profession *"]:::snapshot
    EP --> WP

    W --> WS["[S] wealth_distribution *"]:::snapshot
    N --> WS
    AW --> WS
    W --> GW["[S] gini_wealth *"]:::snapshot
    N --> GW

    WT --> TW["[S] total_wealth *"]:::snapshot

Wealth statistics describe integer consumption tiers rather than monetary assets. GDP is production value added; it does not include the exogenous dependent earnings added to household income. Employment-weighted profession totals are cached once and shared by the wealth summaries and population report. The uniform workforce ratio makes per-capita wealth equal to average wealth.

docs.title: Supply-chain design references
docs.text:
The nominal supply-chain analyzer combines a goods/process graph, constrained optimization, and economic reports. These projects provide useful references for different parts of that design. The comparisons below describe architectural parallels; they do not establish implementation provenance or imply dependencies on these packages.

For usage, see the supply-chain guide. For exact formulas and report boundaries, see the supply-chain data dictionary.

Reference Most relevant design topic Corresponding part of this package Brightway Separate transformations from products. Bipartite graphs, process naming, matrix-backed flows. PyPSA Optimize conversion levels and expose constraint duals. Compiled problems, adjusted rates, constraints and bottlenecks. Calliope Model multiple carriers and shared deployment limits. PM configurations, coproducts, common land/resource budgets. pymrio Trace economic requirements and production factors. Value added, employment, explicit accounting scope. openLCA Make coproduct attribution a modeling choice. Exact process contributions without implicit good-level allocation.

docs.title: Brightway: processes, products, and cycles
docs.text:
Brightway encourages a separate process/product inventory model, while also supporting combined process/product nodes used in existing datasets. A process can have multiple functional edges. This supports our choice to model a complete building/PM configuration as a process, keep goods independent of their producers, and retain every coproduct output. The guide explains why building, method, producer, and recipe name different concepts. Brightway inventory model.

Our physical directions, good → consuming process and process → output good, agree with Brightway's newer interface-schema design. Older Brightway exchange input/output fields do not consistently encode physical direction and should not be mapped directly to our graph roles. Brightway interface schemas, exchange conventions.

Brightway calculates from a technosphere matrix and caches numerical data separately from stored inventory. We similarly use compiled matrices for solving and reports, with cached economy coefficients. Matrix orientation differs: our rows are configurations and columns are goods; Brightway's rows are products and columns are processes. Our owned result snapshots are a project-specific reproducibility choice. Brightway matrix construction.

The terminal target is analogous to product demand in a functional unit, but our quantity is a lower bound on net production. Equal base-price value in a sweep is an economic normalization; it does not establish equivalent product functions. Brightway allows a functional unit containing several products; our analyzer deliberately supports one terminal target per solve. Brightway functional unit.

Brightway Graph Tools describes cyclic supply chains and traversal nodes created for individual visits. Our retained graph instead has one stable node per configuration and measures strongly connected components and condensation depth. Diagram pruning changes presentation without inventing resource leaves. Brightway traversal nodes.

Brightway's standard inventory calculation solves a matrix system for demand; our linear program selects production levels under scenario constraints. Brightway also models biosphere flows and environmental impact characterization. Our game resource flags and economic metrics do not represent environmental impact scores. Brightway calculation and matrix roles.

docs.title: PyPSA: conversions, optimization, and duals
docs.text:
PyPSA's current Process component scales signed input/output rates by one internal dispatch variable. Its Link component also represents conversions with multiple inputs and outputs. This closely parallels our use of one solved configuration level to scale all adjusted goods coefficients. PyPSA's rates scale dispatch; ours specify weekly goods flows per building level, so the units and capacity interpretation differ. PyPSA Process, PyPSA Link.

PyPSA exposes separate model creation and solving methods and maps solution values and constraint duals back to network components. This is a useful parallel for NominalOptimizer.compile(), solve_problem(), and named constraint reporting. We retain raw HiGHS marginals and normalize their signs for objective improvement. bottlenecks() uses binding constraints with useful marginals; a large input cost share alone does not identify a binding limit. PyPSA optimization API.

The analogy concerns conversion coefficients and optimization diagnostics. Our nominal analyzer describes a single weekly production system; it does not implement PyPSA's time-dependent dispatch, storage, or electrical network equations.

docs.title: Calliope: technologies and shared resources
docs.text:
Calliope models technologies with multiple input/output carriers, including coproduction and alternative carriers. It also supports area use tied to technology capacity and a shared available-area constraint. These provide a useful comparison for complete PM configurations with multiple goods and for technologies competing for a common resource budget. Calliope multiple carriers and area constraints.

In our implementation, each PM combination is a separate process with fixed adjusted coefficients. A scenario-wide land cap constrains the combined deployment of all applicable configurations. Per-building limits constrain the combined levels of that building's configurations. The allowed view records static technology eligibility; shared budgets can still make an otherwise allowed route infeasible. The realized view uses the levels chosen by the one optimization solve.

Calliope's carrier and area models are analogies for our goods and land budgets. They do not imply that the analyzer supports carrier switching within one configuration, geographic energy networks, or storage across timesteps.

docs.title: pymrio: demand and economic accounting
docs.text:
pymrio computes industry output from final demand using a Leontief requirement matrix. Its extensions can track production factors such as value added and employment, with direct and indirect requirements and distinct production, consumption, import, and export accounts. This makes it a useful reference for describing what an economic supply-chain metric measures and which boundary it uses. pymrio mathematical background.

Our reports similarly value goods flows and scale employment coefficients by solved production levels. However, system_* includes every solved configuration, while chain_* sums the full contributions of active terminal ancestors, including their coproducts. Those graph-defined totals are not pymrio consumption-based accounts or an allocation of indirect requirements to final demand. Equal-value sweeps compare separate optimized scenarios.

pymrio uses aggregate sector/region input-output relationships. Our model keeps individual production configurations and chooses among them through an LP; it does not calculate a Leontief inverse. A process's whole contribution can belong to several separately analyzed terminal chains, so adding their chain totals can double-count it.

docs.title: openLCA: explicit coproduct allocation
docs.text:
openLCA exposes physical, causal, and economic allocation, as well as system expansion, for processes involving multiple products. Physical allocation uses physical relationships; economic allocation uses cost/revenue relationships; causal allocation requires modeled assumptions. These are distinct policies that can change attribution even when the underlying process is unchanged. openLCA allocation manual.

This illustrates why our API retains exact process-level GDP, employment, and construction contributions without assigning them to output goods. For a process producing two goods, its input cost, employment, and value added are well-defined. How much belongs to each output is an additional modeling decision. Any future good-level allocation needs a named policy, an explicit basis, and reconciliation tests.

openLCA allocates LCA inventories and impacts. It does not provide a default rule for our economic reports. In particular, retaining whole-process contributions in a terminal graph is not a claim that those contributions belong exclusively to that terminal good.
