docs.title: 生产单元排行榜（1.13.11）
docs.text:
时效性

  • 撰写日期： 2026 年 9 月 30 日
  • 游戏数据版本： Victoria 3 1.13.11

后续游戏补丁可能调整建筑、商品基础价格、生产方式和就业结构；重新生成数据表后，本文中的数值与排名也可能随之变化。

docs.title: 生产单元排行榜（1.13.11）
docs.text:
阅读最新版本（1.15） · 1.13.11 存档

在维多利亚3的论坛上，“最强建筑”往往为玩家们津津乐道。根据语境和侧重的不同，结论也通常莫衷一是。是汽车大人？还是工具大人？还是种植园？还是某位神秘世外高人？这次就让我们在 AI 大人的帮助下彻底终结这个话题。

docs.title: 什么是生产单元？
docs.text:
游戏中包含 115 种建筑。每个建筑有若干不同的生产方式。这样，游戏中所有可能的建筑加生产方式组合达到了 1,638 种，我们将其称为生产单元。排除奇观、军队、政府、自给农业、公司总部等建筑，共有 1,274 个值得排名的生产单元。

生产单元决定了输入和输出商品，以及雇佣的人力，提供或消耗的基础设施和建筑力等。

docs.title: 分析口径
docs.text:
在继续下一步之前，首先让我们做一些必要的假设。 1. 市场采用合作社所有制。各生产单元没有人力成本。单元生产商品总值减去单元建筑购买商品总值作为净利润全部直接分红给员工。 2. 市场没有本地市场火星损耗。 3. 忽略市场价格机制，所有商品采用基础价格。这也是最偏离游戏的假设，因此基于这个假设得到的所有指标我会加上“名义”这个前缀来区分。 4. 忽略吞吐量机制，如轧棉机，公司，规模效应等。

有了这些信息，我们可以推算一些我们作为玩家感兴趣的指标。

设一个生产单元的输入商品基础价格总值为 I，输出商品基础价格总值为 O，雇员人数为 L，所需建筑力为 C，则：

  • 名义净利 = O − I
  • 名义人均净利/产值 = (O − I) ÷ L
  • 每点建筑力名义净利 = (O − I) ÷ C

名义净利对应大家熟悉的产值；名义人均净利则对应大家熟悉的人均产值；每点建筑力名义净利与扩张速度和回本周期直接相关。商品流量和名义净利均按周计算；名义净利及人均、每建筑力指标可乘以 52 换算成年值。

排名规则

排名不包含奇观、军队、政府、自给农业、公司总部等非一般商品生产建筑，只保留具有正产出、正就业、正建筑力成本和正名义净利的生产单元。排名对象是生产单元而不是建筑，所以同一建筑的多套生产方式可以同时进入前十。指标相同时，以名义净利更高者优先。

在 AI 的帮助下，我们得到了这张表格，收录了所有生产单元的以上相关信息。让我们根据不同指标排序，看看游戏中有哪些最强生产单元。

docs.title: 尾盘
docs.text: 尾盘排名允许所有生产方式。考虑到后期不在乎回本周期，每点建筑力名义净利就不进行排名了。

docs.title: 名义人均产值
docs.text:
排名 建筑 生产方式组合 时代 名义人均产值 1 武器厂 栓动步枪＋流水线 4 1.140 2 硫矿 柴油泵＋黄色炸药＋辅助蒸汽机＋轨道运输 5 1.037 3 油井 内燃机井架＋罐车 4 1.033 4 武器厂 栓动步枪＋旋转阀发动机 4 0.983 5 工艺装备工坊 机械化钢制工具＋流水线 4 0.975 6 硫矿 柴油泵＋硝化甘油＋辅助蒸汽机＋轨道运输 5 0.960 7 硫矿 柴油泵＋手工钻孔＋辅助蒸汽机＋轨道运输 5 0.957 8 火炮铸造厂 后坐式机制＋流水线 4 0.927 9 铁路 联合内燃机车＋木制乘客车厢 5 0.873 10 汽车厂 大规模生产＋无飞机生产＋无坦克生产＋流水线 5 0.871

万万没想到，有口皆碑的汽车大人，在前十只能垫底。而真神其实也不是我们的武器厂，而是一位世外高人。没错，就是哈瓦那大剧院！区区200学者就能产出5个艺术品，人均高达3.5，可谓一骑绝尘。此外，木制车厢的人均居然超过了科技要求更高的钢制车厢，不得不怀疑P社是否填错了数值。

那么汽车作为人均产值并非最为突出的生产单元，为何会被称为神？无他，唯需求大耳。汽车不仅能满足休闲需求，还能满足自由出行需求，并且在自由出行中的最大供应占比达到 100%；轻武器只能进入休闲需求，适用范围窄得多。火炮则是纯军需品。铁路问题在于运力是本地商品，基本卖不出去。至于硫矿和油井，则是作为资源存在上限。

从这个榜单可以看出几个趋势： - 自动化越激进，人均产值越高。前十生产单元的劳工数量没有超过1,000人的，甚至有些根本不招工人。 - 没有石油，就没有高人均。除了油井，所有前十生产单元都可以说是油老虎。

综上所述，作为人均GDP追求者，最优解其实就是让全国只有一块地，上面盖70座油井或硫矿，同时统御一个巨大的市场，给自己提供名贵工具引擎和消费品。

docs.title: 第三时代：游戏中期
docs.text: 尾盘展示的是上限，但实际经济决策大量发生在游戏中期。现在我们再把科技限制到第三时代，重新运行人均产值和回本周期的榜单。

docs.title: 中期名义人均产值
docs.text:
排名 建筑 生产方式组合 时代 名义人均产值 1 工艺装备工坊 机械化钢制工具＋旋转阀发动机 3 0.683 2 硫矿 冷凝蒸汽机泵＋黄色炸药＋辅助蒸汽机＋轨道运输 3 0.652 3 武器厂 连发步枪＋旋转阀发动机 3 0.650 4 火炮铸造厂 后膛炮＋旋转阀发动机 3 0.631 5 工艺装备工坊 机械化钢制工具＋水管锅炉 3 0.629 6 硫矿 冷凝蒸汽机泵＋硝化甘油＋辅助蒸汽机＋轨道运输 3 0.575 7 硫矿 冷凝蒸汽机泵＋黄色炸药＋手动曲柄起重机＋轨道运输 3 0.541 8 糖料作物种植园 自动灌溉＋离心分晶机＋暴力对待＋轨道运输 3 0.540 9 硫矿 冷凝蒸汽机泵＋手工钻孔＋辅助蒸汽机＋轨道运输 3 0.540 10 硫矿 冷凝蒸汽机泵＋黄色炸药＋辅助蒸汽机＋手推车 3 0.534

人均榜经历了一轮小洗牌。尾盘前十主要依赖第四、第五时代的流水线、柴油泵和内燃机；把上限压到第三时代后，石油直接曼巴 out。然而工具厂、硫矿和军工依旧坚挺。尤其是硫矿靠第2,3生产方式排列组合花式占领了榜首5个席位。糖料种植园靠抽鞭子也爬上了第8名，相对的，铁路则是彻底掉到20名开外。

不夸张地说，橡胶完完全全成就了工具厂的辉煌。如果没有橡胶，工具厂人均产值暴跌至约 0.383，也就是差不多 43.9%，那就废掉了。

docs.title: 中期每点建筑力名义净利
docs.text:
排名 建筑 生产方式组合 时代 每点建筑力名义净利 1 糖料作物种植园 自动灌溉＋离心分晶机＋暴力对待＋手推车 3 15.60 2 糖料作物种植园 自动灌溉＋离心分晶机＋暴力对待＋轨道运输 3 14.85 3 糖料作物种植园 自动灌溉＋蒸汽研磨机＋暴力对待＋手推车 3 13.65 4 糖料作物种植园 基础生产＋离心分晶机＋暴力对待＋手推车 3 13.35 5 糖料作物种植园 自动灌溉＋蒸汽研磨机＋暴力对待＋轨道运输 3 12.90 6 糖料作物种植园 自动灌溉＋离心分晶机＋剥削压榨＋手推车 3 12.60 7 糖料作物种植园 自动灌溉＋真空浓缩罐＋暴力对待＋手推车 3 12.60 8 糖料作物种植园 基础生产＋离心分晶机＋暴力对待＋轨道运输 3 12.60 9 茶叶种植园 自动灌溉＋暴力对待＋手推车 3 12.55 10 糖料作物种植园 自动灌溉＋牛力碾压辊＋暴力对待＋手推车 3 12.00

如果玩家很缺建筑力，只要200锤的种植园几乎是唯一答案。而糖料种植园更是个中翘楚，前十名中居然九个是它的不同生产方式的排列组合，剩下一个是茶叶种植园。但不难看出，流水的生产方式，铁打的鞭子。鞭子好啊，鞭子得抽啊。

如果不抽鞭子，原榜首糖料种植园直接跌至 9.60，下降约 38.5%。而采用电动卷烟机和工厂收音机的烟草种植园则以 11.40 的指标拿下榜首。

到目前的榜单为止，速B也许会看一看，但对于大多数玩家来说，可能并没有种植园可以造，或者玩家想要工业化，而不是把建造力泼在农业上。因此我们追加下面的榜单，只统计工业建筑，看看工业建筑中哪些生产单元回本最快。

docs.title: 中期工业建筑每点建筑力名义净利
docs.text:
只考虑制造业（bg_manufacturing）建筑，包括轻工业、重工业和军事工业，不包括矿山、种植园、铁路、电厂和造船厂。那么第三时代共有 14 种工业建筑、154 个名义盈利的生产单元进入排名。

排名 建筑 生产方式组合 时代 每点建筑力名义净利 1 食品厂 发酵粉＋高效罐头生产＋连续式蒸馏器＋手工面团加工 3 4.42 2 火炮铸造厂 后膛炮＋手工装配 3 4.17 3 工艺装备工坊 机械化钢制工具＋手工装配 3 4.17 4 家具制造厂 机械化工坊＋精密工具＋手工装配 2 4.08 5 武器厂 连发步枪＋手工装配 3 4.00 6 食品厂 发酵粉＋真空包装＋连续式蒸馏器＋手工面团加工 3 3.92 7 食品厂 甜味剂＋高效罐头生产＋连续式蒸馏器＋手工面团加工 3 3.75 8 纺织厂 缝纫机＋弹性织物＋传统织机 3 3.67 9 工艺装备工坊 机械化钢制工具＋水管锅炉 3 3.67 10 食品厂 发酵粉＋高效罐头生产＋罐式蒸馏器＋手工面团加工 3 3.58

食品厂以 4.42 夺冠。不过它同时使用七种投入，并产出 150 单位食品和 100 单位烈酒。烈酒在这里是必要的，它贡献了这个方案总产值的 40%。如果关闭酿酒生产，食品厂的最佳指标会降到 3.33，掉出前十。

工具厂和火炮厂并列第二，余下的则是家具纺织等轻工业和武器厂等军工业。值得注意的是，榜单完全被 600 锤的轻工业和军事工业垄断，而需要 800 锤的化工厂、钢铁厂、发动机厂等重工业无一上榜，毕竟即使重工业的产值不低，除以建筑力后也很难进入前十。

另一个反直觉结果是手工装配大获全胜。工艺装备工坊使用手工装配时为 4.17，换成水管锅炉降至 3.67，换成旋转阀发动机又降至 3.42；火炮铸造厂也从手工装配的 4.17 降到旋转阀发动机的 3.42。这并不表示自动化没有价值，而是因为当前模型不计算工资：自动化减少的雇员在这个指标里不值钱，额外消耗的煤炭和工具却会直接减少名义净利。

docs.title: 总结
docs.text:
纵观四张榜单，我们可以看到，除了跟种植园拼建造力，工具厂和军工厂都能勇夺头筹。左手高产值，右手低雇员。这其中工具的需求又奇高，因此称其为游戏中最夯建筑也不为过。

但值得注意的是，这四张榜单仍然只算了每栋建筑内部的账。每个生产单元表现如何是一回事，其所在产业上下游如何又是另一回事。工具厂这么强，那么会不会被上游的钢铁厂和橡胶园拖累呢？

敬请期待下期维多利亚3全产业链分析。

docs.title: 生产单元排行榜
docs.text:
最新版本：1.15 · 阅读 1.13.11 存档

在维多利亚3的论坛上，“最强建筑”往往为玩家们津津乐道。根据语境和侧重的不同，结论也通常莫衷一是。是汽车大人？还是工具大人？还是种植园？还是某位神秘世外高人？这次就让我们在 AI 大人的帮助下彻底终结这个话题。

docs.title: 相比 1.13.11 的变化
docs.text:
本版沿用原来的指标、筛选条件和时代上限，重新比较 1.15 的生产单元表与固定历史提交中的 1.13.11 生产单元表。

  • 建筑种类由 115 增至 122，生产单元由 1,638 增至 1,731，符合排名条件的生产单元由 1,274 增至 1,328。第三时代制造业的入选单元由 154 增至 158，建筑种类仍为 14。
  • 尾盘前十的成员和顺序不变，但武器厂“栓动步枪＋旋转阀发动机”的名义人均产值由 0.983 降至 0.980。
  • 中期武器厂“连发步枪＋旋转阀发动机”由 0.650 降至 0.647，火炮铸造厂“后膛炮＋旋转阀发动机”由 0.631 降至 0.628。水管锅炉工具厂因此升至第 4，火炮铸造厂降至第 5。
  • 中期每点建筑力名义净利前十的成员、顺序和数值均不变。制造业榜单前九不变，第十由食品厂“发酵粉＋高效罐头生产＋罐式蒸馏器＋手工面团加工”换为家具制造厂“机械化工坊＋高档家具生产＋手工装配”，后者的指标为 3.58。

docs.title: 什么是生产单元？
docs.text:
游戏中包含 122 种建筑。每个建筑有若干不同的生产方式。这样，游戏中所有可能的建筑加生产方式组合达到了 1,731 种，我们将其称为生产单元。排除奇观、军队、政府、自给农业、公司总部等建筑，共有 1,328 个值得排名的生产单元。

生产单元决定了输入和输出商品，以及雇佣的人力，提供或消耗的基础设施和建筑力等。

docs.title: 分析口径
docs.text:
在继续下一步之前，首先让我们做一些必要的假设。

  1. 市场采用合作社所有制。各生产单元没有人力成本。单元生产商品总值减去单元建筑购买商品总值作为净利润全部直接分红给员工。
  2. 市场没有本地市场火星损耗。
  3. 忽略市场价格机制，所有商品采用基础价格。这也是最偏离游戏的假设，因此基于这个假设得到的所有指标我会加上“名义”这个前缀来区分。
  4. 忽略吞吐量机制，如轧棉机，公司，规模效应等。

有了这些信息，我们可以推算一些我们作为玩家感兴趣的指标。

设一个生产单元的输入商品基础价格总值为 I，输出商品基础价格总值为 O，雇员人数为 L，所需建筑力为 C，则：

  • 名义净利 = O − I
  • 名义人均净利/产值 = (O − I) ÷ L
  • 每点建筑力名义净利 = (O − I) ÷ C

名义净利对应大家熟悉的产值；名义人均净利则对应大家熟悉的人均产值；每点建筑力名义净利与扩张速度和回本周期直接相关。商品流量和名义净利均按周计算；名义净利及人均、每建筑力指标可乘以 52 换算成年值。

排名规则

排名不包含奇观、军队、政府、自给农业、公司总部等非一般商品生产建筑，只保留具有正产出、正就业、正建筑力成本和正名义净利的生产单元。排名对象是生产单元而不是建筑，所以同一建筑的多套生产方式可以同时进入前十。指标相同时，以名义净利更高者优先。

在 AI 的帮助下，我们得到了这张表格，收录了所有生产单元的以上相关信息。让我们根据不同指标排序，看看游戏中有哪些最强生产单元。

docs.title: 尾盘
docs.text: 尾盘排名允许所有生产方式。考虑到后期不在乎回本周期，每点建筑力名义净利就不进行排名了。

docs.title: 名义人均产值
docs.text:
排名 建筑 生产方式组合 时代 名义人均产值 1 武器厂 栓动步枪＋流水线 4 1.140 2 硫矿 柴油泵＋黄色炸药＋辅助蒸汽机＋轨道运输 5 1.037 3 油井 内燃机井架＋罐车 4 1.033 4 武器厂 栓动步枪＋旋转阀发动机 4 0.980 5 工艺装备工坊 机械化钢制工具＋流水线 4 0.975 6 硫矿 柴油泵＋硝化甘油＋辅助蒸汽机＋轨道运输 5 0.960 7 硫矿 柴油泵＋手工钻孔＋辅助蒸汽机＋轨道运输 5 0.957 8 火炮铸造厂 后坐式机制＋流水线 4 0.927 9 铁路 联合内燃机车＋木制乘客车厢 5 0.873 10 汽车厂 大规模生产＋无飞机生产＋无坦克生产＋流水线 5 0.871

万万没想到，有口皆碑的汽车大人，在前十只能垫底。而真神其实也不是我们的武器厂，而是一位世外高人。没错，就是哈瓦那大剧院！区区200学者就能产出5个艺术品，人均高达3.5，可谓一骑绝尘。此外，木制车厢的人均居然超过了科技要求更高的钢制车厢，不得不怀疑P社是否填错了数值。

那么汽车作为人均产值并非最为突出的生产单元，为何会被称为神？无他，唯需求大耳。汽车不仅能满足休闲需求，还能满足自由出行需求，并且在自由出行中的最大供应占比达到 100%；轻武器只能进入休闲需求，适用范围窄得多。火炮则是纯军需品。铁路问题在于运力是本地商品，基本卖不出去。至于硫矿和油井，则是作为资源存在上限。

从这个榜单可以看出几个趋势：

  • 自动化越激进，人均产值越高。前十生产单元的劳工数量没有超过1,000人的，甚至有些根本不招工人。
  • 没有石油，就没有高人均。除了油井，所有前十生产单元都可以说是油老虎。

综上所述，作为人均GDP追求者，最优解其实就是让全国只有一块地，上面盖70座油井或硫矿，同时统御一个巨大的市场，给自己提供名贵工具引擎和消费品。

docs.title: 第三时代：游戏中期
docs.text: 尾盘展示的是上限，但实际经济决策大量发生在游戏中期。现在我们再把科技限制到第三时代，重新运行人均产值和回本周期的榜单。

docs.title: 中期名义人均产值
docs.text:
排名 建筑 生产方式组合 时代 名义人均产值 1 工艺装备工坊 机械化钢制工具＋旋转阀发动机 3 0.683 2 硫矿 冷凝蒸汽机泵＋黄色炸药＋辅助蒸汽机＋轨道运输 3 0.652 3 武器厂 连发步枪＋旋转阀发动机 3 0.647 4 工艺装备工坊 机械化钢制工具＋水管锅炉 3 0.629 5 火炮铸造厂 后膛炮＋旋转阀发动机 3 0.628 6 硫矿 冷凝蒸汽机泵＋硝化甘油＋辅助蒸汽机＋轨道运输 3 0.575 7 硫矿 冷凝蒸汽机泵＋黄色炸药＋手动曲柄起重机＋轨道运输 3 0.541 8 糖料作物种植园 自动灌溉＋离心分晶机＋暴力对待＋轨道运输 3 0.540 9 硫矿 冷凝蒸汽机泵＋手工钻孔＋辅助蒸汽机＋轨道运输 3 0.540 10 硫矿 冷凝蒸汽机泵＋黄色炸药＋辅助蒸汽机＋手推车 3 0.534

人均榜经历了一轮小洗牌。尾盘前十主要依赖第四、第五时代的流水线、柴油泵和内燃机；把上限压到第三时代后，石油直接曼巴 out。然而工具厂、硫矿和军工依旧坚挺。尤其是硫矿靠第2,3生产方式排列组合花式占领了榜首5个席位。糖料种植园靠抽鞭子也爬上了第8名，相对的，铁路则是彻底掉到20名开外。

不夸张地说，橡胶完完全全成就了工具厂的辉煌。如果没有橡胶，工具厂人均产值暴跌至约 0.383，也就是差不多 43.9%，那就废掉了。

docs.title: 中期每点建筑力名义净利
docs.text:
排名 建筑 生产方式组合 时代 每点建筑力名义净利 1 糖料作物种植园 自动灌溉＋离心分晶机＋暴力对待＋手推车 3 15.60 2 糖料作物种植园 自动灌溉＋离心分晶机＋暴力对待＋轨道运输 3 14.85 3 糖料作物种植园 自动灌溉＋蒸汽研磨机＋暴力对待＋手推车 3 13.65 4 糖料作物种植园 基础生产＋离心分晶机＋暴力对待＋手推车 3 13.35 5 糖料作物种植园 自动灌溉＋蒸汽研磨机＋暴力对待＋轨道运输 3 12.90 6 糖料作物种植园 自动灌溉＋离心分晶机＋剥削压榨＋手推车 3 12.60 7 糖料作物种植园 自动灌溉＋真空浓缩罐＋暴力对待＋手推车 3 12.60 8 糖料作物种植园 基础生产＋离心分晶机＋暴力对待＋轨道运输 3 12.60 9 茶叶种植园 自动灌溉＋暴力对待＋手推车 3 12.55 10 糖料作物种植园 自动灌溉＋牛力碾压辊＋暴力对待＋手推车 3 12.00

如果玩家很缺建筑力，只要200锤的种植园几乎是唯一答案。而糖料种植园更是个中翘楚，前十名中居然九个是它的不同生产方式的排列组合，剩下一个是茶叶种植园。但不难看出，流水的生产方式，铁打的鞭子。鞭子好啊，鞭子得抽啊。

如果不抽鞭子，原榜首糖料种植园直接跌至 9.60，下降约 38.5%。采用自动灌溉、电动卷烟机、标准条件（或朗读辅助）和手推车的烟草种植园则以 10.80 的指标拿下榜首。

到目前的榜单为止，速B也许会看一看，但对于大多数玩家来说，可能并没有种植园可以造，或者玩家想要工业化，而不是把建造力泼在农业上。因此我们追加下面的榜单，只统计工业建筑，看看工业建筑中哪些生产单元回本最快。

docs.title: 中期工业建筑每点建筑力名义净利
docs.text:
只考虑制造业（bg_manufacturing）建筑，包括轻工业、重工业和军事工业，不包括矿山、种植园、铁路、电厂和造船厂。那么第三时代共有 14 种工业建筑、158 个名义盈利的生产单元进入排名。

排名 建筑 生产方式组合 时代 每点建筑力名义净利 1 食品厂 发酵粉＋高效罐头生产＋连续式蒸馏器＋手工面团加工 3 4.42 2 火炮铸造厂 后膛炮＋手工装配 3 4.17 3 工艺装备工坊 机械化钢制工具＋手工装配 3 4.17 4 家具制造厂 机械化工坊＋精密工具＋手工装配 2 4.08 5 武器厂 连发步枪＋手工装配 3 4.00 6 食品厂 发酵粉＋真空包装＋连续式蒸馏器＋手工面团加工 3 3.92 7 食品厂 甜味剂＋高效罐头生产＋连续式蒸馏器＋手工面团加工 3 3.75 8 纺织厂 缝纫机＋弹性织物＋传统织机 3 3.67 9 工艺装备工坊 机械化钢制工具＋水管锅炉 3 3.67 10 家具制造厂 机械化工坊＋高档家具生产＋手工装配 2 3.58

食品厂以 4.42 夺冠。不过它同时使用七种投入，并产出 150 单位食品和 100 单位烈酒。烈酒在这里是必要的，它贡献了这个方案总产值的 40%。如果关闭酿酒生产，食品厂的最佳指标会降到 3.33，掉出前十。

工具厂和火炮厂并列第二，余下的则是家具纺织等轻工业和武器厂等军工业。值得注意的是，榜单完全被 600 锤的轻工业和军事工业垄断，而需要 800 锤的化工厂、钢铁厂、发动机厂等重工业无一上榜，毕竟即使重工业的产值不低，除以建筑力后也很难进入前十。

另一个反直觉结果是手工装配大获全胜。工艺装备工坊使用手工装配时为 4.17，换成水管锅炉降至 3.67，换成旋转阀发动机又降至 3.42；火炮铸造厂也从手工装配的 4.17 降到旋转阀发动机的 3.40。这并不表示自动化没有价值，而是因为当前模型不计算工资：自动化减少的雇员在这个指标里不值钱，额外消耗的投入商品却会直接减少名义净利。

docs.title: 总结
docs.text:
纵观四张榜单，我们可以看到，除了跟种植园拼建造力，工具厂和军工厂都能勇夺头筹。左手高产值，右手低雇员。这其中工具的需求又奇高，因此称其为游戏中最夯建筑也不为过。

但值得注意的是，这四张榜单仍然只算了每栋建筑内部的账。每个生产单元表现如何是一回事，其所在产业上下游如何又是另一回事。工具厂这么强，那么会不会被上游的钢铁厂和橡胶园拖累呢？

docs.title: How the constraints compose
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    regions[Selected Japanese states] --> resources[Resource building limits]
    regions --> land[Arable land cap]
    resources --> scenario[Scenario]
    land --> scenario
    employment[Employment cap sweep] --> scenario
    scenario --> solver[NominalOptimizer]
    solver --> results[GDP and building levels]

The important implementation pattern is that state-region helpers return ordinary limits consumed by Scenario; the optimizer does not need a country-specific code path. See the optimization guide and optimization API.

docs.title: Equilibrium search over era-5 supply chains
docs.text:
examples/optimize_supply_chain_equilibrium.py loads the transformation matrix directly from era_5_automation/building_levels.csv, trusting the saved input and selecting the hard-coded ALLOWED_CHAIN_GOODS columns. It does not read the adjacent summary.csv. One chain level reproduces a saved recipe targeting £100,000/week of terminal output at base prices. Each trial transforms chain levels into building levels, then solves household wealth, demand, and market prices using the existing equilibrium solver.

Generate inputs with examples/parse.py, examples/production_analysis.py, and examples/supply_chain_compare.py first. The example selects recipes in ALLOWED_CHAIN_GOODS order and includes every configuration used by a selected recipe, including supporting infrastructure outside the terminal graph. It filters unused matrix rows and retains the recipes' production ratios. If an older artifact collection lacks building_levels.csv, rerun uv run python -m examples.supply_chain_compare to generate it. Per-good process reports are no longer used to reconstruct recipes. The example assumes the source recipes use the preset's throughput multiplier of 1; the matrix does not carry throughput metadata. Exported target metadata assumes the preset's £100,000 base-price target; target quantities are derived by dividing that value by each good's base price.

The 20 allowed chains, in vector order, are clothes, furniture, groceries, coal, oil, electricity, glass, services, liquor, tobacco, opium, wine, tea, coffee, transportation, automobiles, luxury_clothes, luxury_furniture, porcelain, and small_arms. Other goods can still be produced by upstream processes or as coproducts within these recipes.

The objective is GDP. The worker cap is one million, the workforce ratio is 0.4. Infrastructure is unconstrained (min_net_infrastructure=None); usage remains a reported diagnostic, and the summary records an empty minimum. The example uses the shared banned building groups, no goods-balance floor, fixed throughput of 1, and no level-dependent economies of scale. The initial vector assigns equal chain levels and scales them to one million workers. Matrix dimensions are derived from the surviving recipes after unused rows are filtered out.

uv run python -m examples.optimize_supply_chain_equilibrium --max-evaluations 100 --max-iterations 10 --log-every 10

Operating losses are funded by default through a proportional tax on cooperative and dependent income, without guaranteeing payroll. Disable it with:

uv run python -m examples.optimize_supply_chain_equilibrium --no-subsidize-operating-losses --max-evaluations 100 --max-iterations 10

The selected policy applies to saved baselines and every restart. --resume uses the current invocation's policy, which defaults to enabled; summary.csv records it in subsidize_operating_losses. Imported calls also default to enabled; use run(..., subsidize_operating_losses=False) to disable it. Unfundable starting or saved mixes still enter the optimizer, whose funding-shortfall penalty guides search toward a fundable recipe mix. An unfunded saved mix cannot become the best solution. Its initial wealth/GDP metrics are empty, and the summary records initial_equilibrium_status=insufficient_income. Only verified, funded equilibria are exported. If no valid result is found within the trial budget, existing exports remain untouched. Other initialization errors still propagate. See tax-funded operating losses.

The default hard trial budget is 20,000 per local search; --log-level WARNING|INFO|DEBUG controls progress verbosity. After each local search, the example reduces loss-making terminal producers' chain levels by --loss-reduction (default 0.5), keeps other levels unchanged, and starts the next search with a fresh trial budget. It does not scale employment back up. The adjustment includes coproduct revenue and uses the existing numerical loss tolerance; upstream profits do not hide terminal-producer losses.

Iteration stops when a search's verified weekly GDP is strictly lower than the preceding search's GDP. Equal GDP continues, with the earliest solution retained on ties. --max-iterations optionally limits the number of completed local searches. Omit it to continue until GDP decreases; an equal-GDP plateau can then continue indefinitely. --loss-reduction 0 disables reductions for every restart.

The example returns the best feasible, freshly verified equilibrium found and writes its solution reports once, after iteration ends. The worse result that triggers stopping is recorded in the summary. A small trial budget can stop during initialization, retaining the baseline with search_success=False. Budget exhaustion does not imply that the equilibrium solver failed or that a global optimum was found. Financial deficits and unaffordable households remain visible diagnostics.

To start the next search from the saved solution and halve loss-making goods' starting chain levels:

uv run python -m examples.optimize_supply_chain_equilibrium --resume --loss-reduction 0.5 --max-evaluations 100 --max-iterations 10

Resume aligns saved levels by good and verifies that the saved recipe matrix matches the current recipes. It re-evaluates the saved solution, then identifies negative operating surplus among each recipe's terminal-good producers, including coproduct revenue. It scales those chains by 1 - loss_reduction and keeps other chain levels unchanged, without scaling employment back up. This changes the starting point; the optimizer can subsequently increase or decrease any allowed chain. The adjusted vector must satisfy scenario constraints. The reduction fraction must be at least 0 and less than 1 and defaults to 0.5. The re-evaluated saved solution remains eligible as the best export. The first new search is compared against this baseline, so a worse first result stops iteration and preserves the saved solution. Use --resume --loss-reduction 0 --max-iterations 1 for a single search starting from the saved vector unchanged. Without --resume, the first search starts from equal chain levels; subsequent searches use the same profitability adjustment as resumed runs. Validation and equilibrium errors propagate before any export is overwritten.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
The separate collection artifacts/analyses/optimization/supply_chain_equilibrium contains:

  • chain_matrix.csv: labeled building-by-chain transformation coefficients.
  • chains.csv: invocation starting levels and best chain levels with recipe normalization targets.
  • buildings.csv: positive building levels and equilibrium finances.
  • market.csv: all goods' buy/sell orders and equilibrium prices.
  • pop.csv: population, wealth, income, expenses, and balances by configuration and profession.
  • goods_buy_packages.csv: wealth-indexed goods baskets, with wealth retained as a CSV column.
  • summary.csv: one row per completed local search, including initial/final metrics, scenario settings, search diagnostics, GDP change, reduction counts, UTC start time, and elapsed seconds. Resumed runs also include iteration zero for the re-evaluated saved baseline, with empty search diagnostics. is_best identifies the exported solution. Every row includes the invocation's completed-search count, total trial evaluations, total elapsed seconds, selected best iteration, optional iteration cap, and stop reason (objective_worsened or max_iterations). Trial totals follow the optimizer's counting convention: initialization counts, but final verification and separate baseline/starting-point evaluations do not.

The committed snapshot was generated with the earlier average_wealth objective. Rerun the example to generate results with the current GDP objective.

Matrix rows use building + "+" + production_method. Columns and chain-level rows use terminal-good keys. Their product reproduces the returned building levels; the building report filters zeros and sorts positive levels. See the guide and column definitions.

docs.title: Supply chains
docs.text:
In the previous chapter, we ranked production units (buildings with certain production methods combinations) by their employment and construction requirements. But in the end, a country's economy cannot be solely based on oil rigs and automobile factories (unless you actually go for it). A world-dominating superpower's economy must be self-sufficient, which means some people must work in less productive production units to produce the upstream goods.

So this time, our analysis focuses on goods. We will find a set of production units, so that overall, the set produces at least a certain amount of a specific good (and maybe some inevitable byproducts) but consumes only labor and construction points, and no other goods at all. We call this set of production units a supply chain.

The supply chain can be visualized as a directed graph, where the nodes are goods and production units, and the edges are the flows of goods between them.

There are multiple implementations of a supply chain, one of which would be optimized for different objectives, such as minimizing employment or construction points. We are here today to find them, with the help of examples/supply_chain_compare.py, which solves for the minimum employment and minimum construction supply chains for every producible good, under different configurations.

The supply-chain guide explains the API and graph model. The data dictionary defines the report columns, units, formulas, and failure behavior.

View examples/supply_chain_compare.py

docs.title: Methodology
docs.text:
To normalize the comparison, each supply chain has a weekly target base value of £100,000 of its corresponding terminal good, with target quantity calculated as 100_000 / base_price. This is fixed export demand with a zero goods-balance floor and no imports. Surplus and coproducts are possible, so equal target value does not imply equal GDP or make goods interchangeable.

The following table summarizes the three scenarios used in the comparison, with their objectives and additional restrictions. The cangshulun preset, originating from this video, bans certain oil-using production methods to represent the resource constraints. Monuments, ownership buildings and government buildings are also banned in all configurations, as they are not part of the production chain.

Configuration Objective Technology and additional restrictions era_3_construction Minimum whole-system construction Era 3 era_5_automation Minimum whole-system employment Era 5 cangshulun Minimum whole-system employment Era 5, CANGSHULUN_BANNED_PMS, and CANGSHULUN_BUILDING_LIMITS

Note that the above constraints do not simulate every in-game law, qualification, or state-specific PM restriction. These are idealized model requirements, with no wage costs or profession availability constraints.

A failed solve produces a configuration-summary row with its requested target, status, and error text, and the script continues to the next configuration and good. Failed configurations have no detailed reports or plots. Unknown goods, duplicate good keys, and invalid base prices raise before any output is written.

docs.title: The automobile supply chain
docs.text:
The employment and construction requirements for the automobile supply chain under different scenarios are summarized in the following table.

Configuration Status Employment (workers) Construction (points) Era 3 construction Infeasible Unavailable Unavailable Era 5 automation Success 125,161 25,217.7 Cangshulun Success 138,218 27,713.7

The £100,000 target corresponds to 1,000 automobiles per week. Both successful cases produce £100,000 of weekly value added, or £5.2 million annually, while using different amounts of labor and construction. In this example, whole-system and terminal-chain totals agree; that equality is not a general guarantee of the API.

Within analyses/supply_chains/era_5_automation/automobiles/, the reports explain where those requirements come from:

  • goods.csv and goods_balance.svg compare supply, consumption, imports, and net production. The terminal production floor is a separate constraint, rather than a population or export buy order.
  • processes.csv identifies the selected building/PM configurations and their levels. flows.csv records process inputs and outputs.
  • workforce.csv and workforce.svg describe employment by profession. Minimizing total employment does not necessarily minimize skilled labor.
  • constraints.csv, bottlenecks.csv, and constraints.svg expose LP diagnostics and useful binding inequalities. Marginals are local and objective-specific, and constraints can have different units.
  • alternatives.csv lists all allowed producer configurations, including inactive ones. The diagrams can prune alternatives for readability.

Era 5 automation: automobile-chain goods balance, in units per week.

Era 5 automation: binding automobile-chain constraints, measured in workers saved per relaxed constraint unit.

docs.title: Compare contributions
docs.text:
contributions_gdp.svg, contributions_employment.svg, and contributions_construction_cost.svg show leading whole-process contributions to the terminal chain. The same process can matter very differently for labor, construction, and value added.

Era 5 automation: leading automobile-chain contributions to weekly value added (£).

Era 5 automation: leading automobile-chain employment contributions, in workers.

Era 5 automation: leading automobile-chain construction contributions, in construction points.

For the era 5 automobile chain, automotive assembly employs 70,000 workers and requires 16,000 construction points. The upstream chain therefore accounts for another 55,161 workers. Rubber plantations employ about 16,392 workers but require only 655.7 construction points; oil rigs employ 15,590 workers and require 2,078.7 points. Their relative importance changes between the employment and construction charts. Machinists and engineers together account for 73.9% of chain employment, which illustrates why a small total workforce can still depend heavily on skilled professions.

Era 5 automation: automobile-chain workforce by profession, in workers.

Chain totals include whole selected processes, including their coproducts; they do not allocate a factory's workers or construction uniquely to one good. Whole-system totals can also include activity outside the graph-defined chain. Weekly value added is output base value minus intermediate input base cost; annual GDP is 52 times weekly GDP.

docs.title: Goods & scenario sweep
docs.text:
The combined summary is artifacts/analyses/supply_chains/comparison/summary.csv. It contains one row per good/configuration pair selected in the current run, in requested good order and then configuration order. It retains failures. Each configuration has one summary.csv combining its selected goods, for example analyses/supply_chains/era_5_automation/summary.csv. It records each good's target, objective, solver status, whole-system totals, chain totals, and configuration labels. No summary files are written inside the individual good directories. Use a single configuration when ranking goods under common assumptions.

The comparison directory contains this summary and three grouped bar charts:

  • pop.svg plots system_employment, the whole-system employed population in workers. It excludes dependents and unemployed people.
  • construction_points.svg plots system_construction_cost in construction points.
  • gdp_per_capita.svg plots system_gdp_per_capita_annual: annual system GDP divided by system employment, in £ per worker per year. Zero employment gives zero, matching the economy model's GDP-per-capita convention.

from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd

comparison = pd.read_csv(
    Path("artifacts/analyses/supply_chains/comparison/summary.csv")
)
successful = comparison.loc[
    comparison["configuration"].eq("era_5_automation")
    & comparison["status"].eq("success")
]
lowest_employment = successful.sort_values(
    ["system_employment", "good"], kind="stable"
).head(10)

Sorting the automation rows by construction answers which of those minimum-employment chains uses least construction. It does not compute a minimum-construction optimum for each good.

docs.title: Reproducing Cangshulun's video
docs.text:
Apart from the video mentioned above, the uploader also made a follow-up video running a complete supply chain analysis for all goods on the 1.12 patch. His methodology is not mathematic programming, but rather a leontief matrix approach, where production units are selected manually. To reproduce his results, the examples/supply_chain_cangshulun.py script adds throughput bonuses, production-method bans, and named product variants to approximate the video's assumptions.

uv run python -m examples.supply_chain_cangshulun

The script writes the latest complete results to artifacts/analyses/supply_chains/cangshulun_video/summary.csv. The frozen artifacts/analyses/supply_chains/cangshulun_video/summary_1.12.csv contains 60 scenarios from the 1.12.5 results, extracted from artifact commit e7a3748964cf28f453db1899f08636eb04c45d71 and sorted by annual value added per worker. It retains only the columns used for the video comparison:

  • scenario
  • system_gdp_annual
  • system_employment
  • system_gdp_per_capita_annual
  • system_levels_per_10k_pop_building_sulfur_mine
  • system_levels_per_10k_pop_building_coal_mine
  • system_levels_per_10k_pop_building_iron_mine
  • system_levels_per_10k_pop_building_lead_mine
  • system_levels_per_10k_pop_building_logging_camp
  • system_levels_per_10k_pop_building_rubber_plantation
  • system_levels_per_10k_pop_building_oil_rig

The video's table at 1:04 is reproduced below. Its total value column is weekly, so compare it with system_gdp_annual / 52; its per-worker value is annual and corresponds to system_gdp_per_capita_annual. Resource columns measure building levels per 10,000 employed workers. Our runs target £100,000 of weekly terminal output, so raw value and employment totals have a different scale from the screenshot; compare the per-worker and per-10,000-worker ratios.

docs.title: Output inventory
docs.text:
Paths are relative to --output-dir. All text outputs use UTF-8 without a BOM. The comparison writes one detailed result at a time rather than retaining all goods' graphs and snapshots in memory.

Directory Files analyses/supply_chains/era_3_construction/<good>/ Detailed files below for successful solves analyses/supply_chains/era_5_automation/<good>/ Same reports, plots, and diagrams analyses/supply_chains/cangshulun/<good>/ Same reports, plots, and diagrams analyses/supply_chains/<configuration>/ summary.csv, combining that configuration's selected goods, and building_levels.csv, the complete production-unit levels for each selected good analyses/supply_chains/comparison/ summary.csv, pop.svg, construction_points.svg, gdp_per_capita.svg, covering all selected goods and presets analyses/supply_chains/cangshulun_video/ Latest complete summary.csv and frozen selected-column summary_1.12.csv; ordinary generation updates only summary.csv

Each successful comparison configuration contains goods.csv, processes.csv, flows.csv, workforce.csv, constraints.csv, bottlenecks.csv, alternatives.csv, supply_chain_recipe.mmd, supply_chain_realised.mmd, network.svg, goods_balance.svg, workforce.svg, constraints.svg, contributions_gdp.svg, contributions_employment.svg, and contributions_construction_cost.svg. Headline metrics and failure rows are stored only in the configuration-level summary.csv and comparison CSVs.

The configuration summary and comparison CSVs use the public sweep schema, plus configuration and ban_config. GDP efficiency and per-building resource levels, including levels per 10,000 employed workers, are public summary fields shared with the video export. The other detailed CSVs retain their public report schemas. Cross-good summaries sit at configuration level. A selected-good run replaces the configuration summaries and combined comparison with that run's selection; other goods' directories remain. Each configuration's building_levels.csv is also replaced for that selection. Its first column, config, identifies the building and PM combination, followed by one column per selected good. Unused production units have zero levels; failed solves have blank cells throughout their good's column.
